articles.title: Red rainfall warning up over parts of Zambales, Bataan
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) raised a red rainfall warning over parts of Zambales and Bataan as of 8 a.m. on Friday,…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) raised a red rainfall warning over parts of Zambales and Bataan as of 8 a.m. on Friday, Sept. 4 amid rains brought by the southwest monsoon, or “habagat.”
The warning covers San Narciso, San Felipe, San Marcelino, Castillejos, San Antonio, Subic and Olongapo in Zambales, as well as Dinalupihan in Bataan.
The red warning means rainfall of at least 30 millimeters (mm) is expected within an hour, which could cause serious flooding in vulnerable areas.
An orange rainfall warning was raised over the following areas:

items: Zambales (Botolan, Cabangan, Candelaria, Iba, Masinloc, Palauig, and Santa Cruz)
Bataan (Abucay, Bagac, Balanga, Limay, Mariveles, Morong, Orani, Orion, Pilar, Samal, and Hermosa); and
Bulacan (Hagonoy, Calumpit, Paombong, Malolos, Plaridel, Pulilan, Guiguinto, Balagtas, Baliuag, Bustos, Pandi, Angat, and Bulakan)

blocks.text: The orange warning indicates that rainfall between 15 mm and 30 mm is expected within an hour and may last up to two hours, which may bring “threatening” flooding in vulnerable areas.
A yellow rainfall warning was also raised over the following areas:

items: Bulacan (Bocaue, Meycauayan, San Jose del Monte, Dona Remedios Trinidad, Marilao, Norzagaray, Obando, San Ildefonso, San Miguel, San Rafael, and Santa Maria)
Laguna (Cabuyao, Santa Rosa, Binan, San Pedro), Batangas(Laurel, Lemery, Calaca, Balayan, Tuy, Nasugbu, Lian, and Calatagan); and
Nueva Ecija (Cuyapo, Nampicuan, Guimba, Licab, Zaragoza, San Antonio, and Cabiao)

blocks.text: The yellow warning indicates that rainfall between 7.5 mm and 15 mm is expected within an hour and may last up to two hours, which may likewise bring flooding in vulnerable areas.
Meanwhile, Pagasa said light to moderate with occasional heavy rains were expected over the following areas on Friday morning:

items: Quezon (Candelaria, Dolores, San Antonio, Sariaya, Tiaong, General Nakar, Tayabas, Infanta, Lucban, Lucena, Mauban, Pagbilao, Real, Sampaloc, Agdangan, Atimonan, Burdeos, Jomalig, Padre Burgos, Panukulan, Patnanungan, Plaridel, Polillo, Perez, Alabat, and Quezon)

Laguna (Alaminos, Bay, Calauan, Calamba, Liliw, Los Banos, Luisiana, Magdalena, Majayjay, Nagcarlan, Pagsanjan, Pila, Rizal, San Pablo, Santa Cruz, Victoria, Cavinti, Famy, Kalayaan, Lumban, Mabitac, Paete, Pakil, Pangil, Santa Maria, and Siniloan)

Batangas (Agoncillo, Alitagtag, Balete, Batangas City, Bauan, Tanauan, Cuenca, Ibaan, Lipa, Lobo, Mabini, Malvar, Mataasnakahoy, Padre Garcia, Rosario, San Jose, San Juan, San Luis, San Nicolas, San Pascual, Santa Teresita, Santo Tomas, Taal, Talisay, Taysan, and Tingloy); and

articles.title: U.S. aims 'to really tighten the screws' on Cuba with newest sanctions: analyst
articles.summary: The U.S. government on Thursday slapped new sanctions on Cuba in a fresh push to strangle the island's economy and deepen its multiple crises.

image.caption: A man pulls a cart carrying drinking water along a street in Havana last month. On Thursday, the U.S. government slapped new sanctions on Cuba in a fresh push to strangle the island's economy and deepen its multiple crises. (Ramon Espinosa/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New
The U.S. government on Thursday slapped new sanctions on Cuba in a fresh push to strangle the island's economy and deepen its multiple crises.
Company that imports parts needed to maintain Cuba's power grid among those hit with sanctions

Among those hit with sanctions are Fidel Ernesto Castro, grandson of former president Raúl Castro, and Cuba's Oil Industry Supply Import Co., known as Abapet. The company is responsible for importing special equipment and spare parts needed to sustain Cuba's crumbling power grid.

The sanctions aim to push Cuba's critical machinery offline and exacerbate its energy crisis, said Brett Erickson, a sanctions expert and managing principal at Obsidian Risk Advisors, a consulting firm.
"The U.S. is trying to really tighten the screws as much as possible," he said.

"The Trump administration seems to have no seriousness to accept any change from Cuba other than a toppling of regime. Marco is not going to let that go," he added, referring to U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
Erickson anticipated that Cuba's government would try to circumvent the sanctions "because they have to."
"They'll get creative in how they try to procure these maintenance parts," he said, warning it would be a costlier alternative, which in turn would raise inflation and further hurt Cuba's economy.
Frequent outages, fuel reserves dwindling

Islandwide blackouts have become increasingly common, while daily outages in Cuba now surpass 24 hours as the aging grid fails and fuel reserves dwindle ever since U.S. President Donald Trump in late January threatened tariffs on any country that sells or provides oil to the island.

"The goal in theory is to create so much civilian hardship and suffering that they have no option but to essentially rise up and topple their government," Erickson said. "It is an attempt to cause a humanitarian crisis."
Talks earlier this year between the U.S. and Cuba have since halted, while sanctions have increased in recent months.

Erickson said he expects the U.S. to keep targeting smaller and smaller state companies to try to push them "into a death spiral." The U.S. has previously sanctioned entities including Cuba's state-owned oil and gas company.
LISTEN | Cuba and fears of a U.S. invasion:
Front Burner32:39Will the U.S. invade Cuba?
The U.S. State Department made the announcement just hours after Cuban officials held a press conference to share more details on the historic economic reforms approved in June.
When asked about the current situation in Cuba, Oscar Pérez-Oliva Fraga, Cuba's deputy prime minister and minister of foreign investment, blamed the U.S. government.
"This past year has been very complex, and we know why," he said. "The blockade is a genocide."
He spoke before the sanctions were announced.
No sense of 'what's going to happen to you'

Among the Cubans exhausted by the ongoing outages is 49-year-old Yaqueline Bernal. She said Thursday that she hasn't had electricity since Sunday and worries most about the consequences for her eight young grandchildren.
"If we don't have power, we don't have water," she said. "You really don't know what's going to happen to you."
Bruno Rodríguez, Cuba's foreign affairs minister, decried the latest sanctions on X.

"Collective punishment is a crime. So, too, is inflicting suffering on an entire population through measures coldly calculated to trigger a humanitarian crisis," he said. "Enough with the abuse. Put an end to the blockade once and for all and allow Cuba to live in peace."
Eugenio Martínez Enríquez, Cuba's ambassador in Mexico, called Rubio "a liar without scruples."
"We will not forget his crimes," he wrote on X.
Meanwhile, Rubio asserted on X that those sanctioned "are part of the corrupt Castro financial and intelligence network."

"Cuba's Communist regime elites preside over a failed state where ordinary Cubans go hungry while the Castro family and other insiders enrich themselves through sanctions evasion and other illicit schemes — and seek to export subversive Marxist ideology to the United States and other states in the Western Hemisphere," he wrote.
"Trump and I are unwavering in our commitment that Cuba will be free."

articles.title: Global Affairs collecting DNA from families of Canadians missing in Nepal
articles.summary: Federal government officials said Global Affairs Canada is working to collect DNA from the families of Canadians still missing in Nepal and China after a flash flood ripped through the border region…

image.caption: An aerial view shows houses standing amid debris during a helicopter flight from Nuwakot to Rasuwa following the deadly flash floods and mudslides in Nepal. Officials are searching for hundreds of missing people, including 29 Canadians. (Navesh Chitrakar/Reuters)

blocks.text: Canada

Federal government officials said Global Affairs Canada is working to collect DNA from the families of Canadians still missing in Nepal and China after a flash flood ripped through the border region last week.
There are 29 Canadians unaccounted for following flash flooding last week

Senior government officials, briefing reporters on background, said they are starting to collect the samples from the families of 29 people still considered missing, with assistance from the RCMP and police forces in Nepal and China.
The flooding on Aug. 26 killed more than 1,100 people and left roughly 4,400 missing after a glacier collapsed in the Himalayan border region between Nepal and China.
In Kathmandu, police have buried dozens of unidentified bodies in trenches because there are too many to keep or identify individually.
Canadian located safe
One Canadian was found safe, while the remaining 29 are believed to have been in the region where the flash flood occurred.
The Nepal Tourism Board reported on Sept. 1 that more than 580 foreign nationals and tourists were still unaccounted for, while another 330 had been rescued.
Federal officials said the situation is changing by the day and they continue to work with local authorities and the families of the missing.
Global Affairs has 10 officials in Kathmandu and has established points of contact with the families of the missing Canadians.
Search, recovery and identification efforts are being led by Nepali and Chinese authorities and Canada has offered assistance, the federal officials said.

articles.title: Trump names Adam Telle as acting army secretary following the departure of Driscoll
articles.summary:
Telle has previously worked for Trump during his first term as a special assistant to the president for legislative affairs

Donald Trump on Thursday named Adam Telle as the acting army…

blocks.text: Donald Trump on Thursday named Adam Telle as the acting army secretary after the departure of Daniel Driscoll amid widespread reports of tensions with defense secretary Pete Hegseth.
Telle is currently the assistant secretary of the army for civil works.
“He is a Great Patriot, who is respected by all,” the US president wrote in a Truth Social post.

Driscoll gave no explanation for his decision to quit this week as the army’s top civilian official. His clashes with Hegseth have been widely reported, and some of Driscoll’s allies in the army were ousted this year by Trump’s Pentagon chief.

Telle has been at the Army Office of Civil Works since August 2025, according to Legistorm, a website that tracks lawmakers and Capitol Hill staffers. Before that, Telle spent 20 years mostly working in Congress for lawmakers, including as chief of staff for Republican Senator Bill Hagerty of Tennessee from 2021 to 2025.

Telle had a job for 18 months working in the White House during Trump’s first term as a special assistant to the president for legislative affairs, Legistorm said. He also spent more than 10 years working for the late Republican Senator Thad Cochran of Mississippi.
Telle will be overseeing the country’s largest fighting force at a time when the US is still engaged in conflict with Iran and significant army forces are stationed in the Middle East.

The war has significantly contributed to the US military’s shortfall in critical weapons like the Patriot and Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (Thaad) missile interceptor systems, which are operated by the army.
Driscoll, an army veteran who served in Iraq, did not offer an explanation for why he stepped down after 18 months as the service’s civilian leader.

He is a friend of vice-president JD Vance and had good relationships with both Republicans and Democrats in Congress. His allies in the army who were ousted by Hegseth included its top uniformed leader, Gen Randy George.
Gen Christopher LaNeve took over as the army’s acting chief of staff and recently pulled the plug on a drone modernization program that Driscoll had championed.
Driscoll spoke with Trump on the current state of the army before he submitted his resignation, the Associated Press has reported.
Driscoll did not allude to any problems in the only public statement on his departure, saying Tuesday that it has been “the honor of a lifetime” to serve as army secretary under Trump and Hegseth.
“We could not have made the progress we did without the support of secretary Hegseth,” he added.
Democrats and Republicans lamented Driscoll’s departure, with some blaming Hegseth directly.
Sen Thom Tillis, a North Carolina Republican who is retiring and sometimes has clashed with Trump, said on social media that Hegseth “is creating a leadership void at the top of our military ranks”.

articles.title: Parts of NLEx in San Simon remain flooded Friday, Sept. 4
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Parts of the Northern Luzon Expressway (NLEx), particularly in San Simon, Pampanga, remain flooded on Friday, September 4. In an advisory on the road and traffic conditions on…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Parts of the Northern Luzon Expressway (NLEx), particularly in San Simon, Pampanga, remain flooded on Friday, September 4.

In an advisory on the road and traffic conditions on the expressway at 7 a.m., the NLEx Corporation said water build-up was still present on all northbound and southbound lanes at the San Simon interchange area.
It added that a traffic build-up of 200 meters had been observed on the southbound lanes at the San Simon interchange, while a traffic build-up of 50 meters had been observed on the northbound lanes.

Only the first northbound and southbound lanes at the San Simon interchange were passable to all types of vehicles, while the second northbound and southbound lanes were only passable to class 2 and 3 vehicles, which are larger vehicles including buses and trucks.
Meanwhile, the third northbound and southbound lanes at the San Simon interchange were not passable, the advisory noted.
Likewise, the NLEx Corporation said water build-up was observed in all northbound lanes and the third southbound lane of the expressway in the Tulaoc area.
It added that only the first and second northbound and southbound lanes were passable to all types of vehicles, while the third northbound and southbound lanes were not passable.
Only light traffic was observed in the Tulaoc area.

The NLEx Corporation also noted that the Santa Rita northbound entry, the Balagtas northbound entry and the Pulilan northbound lanes; as well as the southbound lanes in Balintawak and Valenzuela were passable to all types of vehicles as of its posting.
It added that the Libtong exit in Meycauayan, Bulacan was temporarily closed.
The flooding and heavy traffic had developed amid persistent torrential rains in the region over the past week, prompting public frustration.

In a statement last Monday, NLEx operator Metro Pacific Tollways Corporation sympathized with the public, stressing that it was “deeply sorry” for the hours-long delays motorists endured and committing to deploy concrete barriers and siphoning trucks to alleviate the situation. /jpv

articles.title: Iran buries victims of reported US wedding attack, fires on Kuwait
articles.summary: The US is investigating the incident and would learn from any mistakes made by its military, says Vice President JD Vance

blocks.text: INJURED. An injured victim lies in a hospital bed following an attack at a wedding near Sirik, a coastal area on the Strait of Hormuz, the Iranian Red Crescent reported, as the United States and Iran engaged in the most significant exchange of fire in weeks, in Sirik, Hormozgan province, Iran, September 2, 2026, in this screen grab taken from a handout video.
via REUTERS
The US is investigating the incident and would learn from any mistakes made by its military, says Vice President JD Vance

items: Iranian mourners held a funeral for victims of a US airstrike that reportedly struck a wedding party, resulting in five deaths and nearly 70 injuries.

In retaliation, Iran launched missiles and drones at a US base in Kuwait, marking the largest escalation in the conflict in over a month, while US officials stated they were investigating the incident.
The airstrikes have caused a spike in oil prices, and despite the recent violence, the month of August had been relatively quiet in the Gulf following a halt in US airstrikes.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

DUBAI, UAE – Iranian mourners carried caskets at a funeral on Thursday, September 3, for victims of a US airstrike said to have struck a wedding party, and Tehran launched missiles and drones overnight at a US base in Kuwait, after the war’s biggest escalation in more than a month.

Mourners assembled in the late afternoon outside the village of Kuhestak in Sirik County, along a stretch of the Strait of Hormuz coast that was hit by heavy US airstrikes late on Tuesday, September 1.

Iranian state television on Thursday said that a 22-year-old woman had died in hospital following the strike that hit a home during a wedding, taking the total reported death toll to five. Iranian officials said that nearly 70 were wounded.

blocks.caption: US launches new strikes on Iran as Tehran hits back in widening conflict

blocks.text: US Vice President JD Vance told reporters on Thursday that the United States was looking into the incident.

“We’re investigating it because obviously we care. We want to know,” he said. “If we do make mistakes, again, this is a big difference between us and Iran, when our military makes mistakes, they learn from them to try to get better from them,” Vance added.
The US military said it was aware of the Iranian reports but it “never targets civilians.”

At the funeral for four victims from the wedding, Iran’s Mehr news agency video showed a pickup truck carrying a flag-draped coffin beneath a canopy of palm fronds. A reporter in front of the truck said, “This is the body of Martyr Amir-Mohammad Karimi, a 4-year-old child who was martyred in an attack on the country’s south by the criminal American regime.”
In other footage of the funeral, mourners threw petals into the air as doleful music played from a loudspeaker. A casket was carried past a row of soldiers standing at attention with rifles.
“If it was a military location, it wouldn’t be so painful. This was a wedding ceremony, but they turned people’s joy into mourning,” the semi-official Tasnim news agency quoted a local man as saying.
Washington launched the airstrikes on Tuesday, hitting what it said were military targets along the coast in retaliation for Iranian attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

The sudden escalation of the Iran war has caused a surge in oil prices to levels unseen since July. Prices rose for a fourth straight day on Thursday, taking Brent crude futures LCOc1 over $96 a barrel.

Iran reported 18 dead in the last US assault. It responded on Wednesday to the US strikes with attacks on US bases in Iraq, Jordan, Qatar, Kuwait and Bahrain, and carried out further attacks early on Thursday, saying it was targeting another US base, in Kuwait.

Kuwait’s military said its air defenses had intercepted missiles and drones. But following that, the war’s biggest flareup since July appeared to subside, with no more major attacks from either side reported as Thursday wore on.

The month of August was largely quiet in the Gulf after US President Donald Trump abruptly halted two weeks of intensive airstrikes in July, having been warned by his military that Washington was running low on munitions.

Trump has yet to achieve the aims he set out when he launched Operation Epic Fury in February: to end Iran’s nuclear program, halt its ability to attack its neighbors and create conditions for Iranians to topple their leadership.

Iran’s economy has suffered severely from a US blockade. But its clerical rulers remain in power and aim to emerge from the war stronger than before, demanding the lifting of sanctions and hoping to collect fees from ships that use the strait, which carried a fifth of global oil and gas shipments before the war. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Split verdict in New Orleans murder trial tied to staged-wrecks scheme
articles.summary:
Sean Alfortish and Leon Parker convicted on some counts but not murder charges linked to insurance fraud plot

A federal jury in New Orleans on Thursday returned a split verdict after more…

blocks.text: A federal jury in New Orleans on Thursday returned a split verdict after more than 30 hours of deliberations in a three-week-long blockbuster fraud and murder trial that garnered headlines far beyond Louisiana.

Jurors deadlocked on murder charges Sean Alfortish and Leon “Chunky” Parker faced, leading US district judge Wendy Vitter to declare a mistrial as prosecutors vowed to try the case on those counts again.

“Today’s verdict is an important step towards justice,” US attorney David Courcelle of the eastern district of Louisiana said at a Thursday press conference. “Alfortish and Parker exploited the courts to benefit themselves and confederates.”

Alfortish was found guilty of conspiracy to commit mail and wire fraud, two counts of mail fraud, obstruction of justice, and witness tampering. He was found not guilty of another count of obstruction of justice and subornation of perjury.

Jurors were not able to reach verdicts on charges Alfortish and Parker faced of conspiracy to commit witness tampering through murder, witness tampering through murder, conspiracy to retaliate against a witness through murder, retaliation against a witness through murder and causing death through use of a firearm.
That means the jury was not able to reach a unanimous verdict.
Vitter declared a mistrial on the five murder-related counts against Alfortish and Parker.
Alfortish faces 90 years in prison. Parker, who previously pleaded guilty to conspiracy and two counts of mail fraud, faces up to 60 years.

Dubbed “Operation Sideswipe”, more than 63 people have previously been convicted in the massive scheme that involved so-called “slammers” who would get into accidents with 18-wheelers to file fraudulent insurance claims.
The unresolved charges center on the killing of Cornelius Garrison, who prosecutors said was cooperating with the FBI in its investigation into the staged-crash scheme.

Prosecutors accused Alfortish and Parker of conspiring to kill Garrison in the front door of his mother’s home after learning he was talking to federal investigators. Prosecutors also alleged Alfortish paid Parker to carry out the killing.

“They brought every resource of the federal government that they could bring. They brought five assistant US attorneys on to the case. They had a phalanx of FBI agents. They tried in every way possible to convict Sean Alfortish of murdering a federal informant. And the jury did not find in their favor,” Shaune Clarke, Alforitsh’s attorney, told reporters after the verdict.
“They couldn’t prove it this time. And they’re not going to be able to prove it the next time because it isn’t true. It didn’t happen.”

“We’re appreciative of the jury refusing to convict on this evidence, which we think was an appropriate decision, and I’ll leave it at that,” Stephen Haedicke, Parker’s attorney, said on the courthouse steps.

articles.title: Volkswagen to cut 100,000 jobs by end of decade
articles.summary: The company will carry out the biggest job cuts ever seen in the industry. Volkswagen also plans to restructure and invest in research.

image.caption: Volkswagen's Zwickau plant is expected to be affected by the cuts [FILE: June 2026]Image: Hendrik Schmidt/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: German automobile giant Volkswagenannounced on Thursday that it would be cutting a total of 100,000 jobs by the end of the decade in what is set to be the biggest restructuring ever seen in the global car industry.
The company said that management and trade unions had approved a plan involving the reduction of a further 50,000 jobs, in addition to 50,000 redundancies already agreed.
"It is essential to systematically align workforce levels with economic realities," read a statement from the multi-brand Volkswagen group which, apart from VW itself, also includes Audiand Porsche.
The total of 100,000 cuts amount to about 15% of Volkswagen staff worldwide. The cull eclipses the 50,000 job cuts General Motors made after it declared bankruptcy in 2009.

Unions and management had publicly rowed before signing off on the plans, with the former accusing the latter of not been honest with the workforce after the figure of 100,000 possible job cuts surfaced in the media before being communicated internally.
'The motor of the entire region'

What's more, Volkswagen also said the long-term future of four major German plants – in Hannover, Emden, Zwickau and Neckarsulm — could not be guaranteed. Their closure would mark the first full-scale shuttering of Volkswagen factories in its home country.
"If this plant really were shut down, you could put a big black spot on the map," one long-term employee in Zwickau, Saxony, told the AFP news agency.
"The plant and the jobs outside it, our suppliers, they're the motor of the entire region."
Caught between US tariffs, Chinese competition and a sluggish growth in demand for electric vehicles, Europe's largest carmaker is in trouble.
Company reforms to drive profitability
However, CEO Oliver Blume insisted that the decision to cut 100,000 jobs sent "a strong signal for the future of the Volkswagen Group."

blocks.caption: Volkswagen CEO Oliver Blume said that the company will take responsibility for its entire workforce, its partners, and industrial jobs worldwide [FILE: March 2026]Image: Julian Stratenschulte/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Volkswagen did not give details as to the timing of the cuts and how they would be distributed across the different regions where it has plants and offices, but the company said its focus will turn to North America and that it is looking to expand exports to the Global South.
The plan also includes a three-digit-billion sum investment over the coming years as VW looks to improve technologically through research and development and become more competitive.
Among the moves is a structural change that should bring about faster decision-making and a cut to the number of businesses and holdings it owns by about one-third.
Volkswagen's crisis: How many jobs are at risk?

articles.title: Pagasa: Habagat rains to drench parts of Luzon on Friday, Sept. 4
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) said the southwest monsoon, locally known as habagat, will bring rains over parts of…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) said the southwest monsoon, locally known as habagat, will bring rains over parts of Luzon on Friday, September 4.

“Ngayong araw, inaasahan natin na posible na magtuloy-tuloy ang kung minsan yung malalakas nga ng mga pag-ulan dulot ng habagat,” Pagasa weather specialist Obet Badrina said in the agency’s forecast on Friday morning.
(Today, we expect occasional heavy rains to prevail due to the southwest monsoon.)
“Dito nga sa Luzon, inaasahan natin yung malalakas ng mga pag-ulan dito sa may bahagi ng Bataan at Zambales,” he added.
(Here in Luzon, we expect heavy rains in Bataan and Zambales.)
Metro Manila, Southern Luzon and the remaining parts of Central Luzon will experience occasional rains, according to the forecaster.

Meanwhile, the rest of Luzon as well as the western portion of the Visayas can expect cloudy weather conditions with chances of localized rain showers and thunderstorms in the afternoon and evening, Badrina noted.

“Sa ibang bahagi naman ng Kabisayaan, sa Central Visayas at Eastern Visayas, ay mas maaliwalas ang panahon na maranasan sa araw na ito, bagamat posible pa rin yung mga pulu-pulong mga pag-ulan, pagkidlat at pagkulog,” he said.
(In other parts of the Visayas, particularly Central Visayas and Eastern Visayas, the weather is fairer today, although there is still the possibility of isolated rain showers and thunderstorms.)
“Ang kalakhang Mindanao naman, inaasahan pa rin natin ang maaliwalas sa panahon, bagamat posible pa rin yung mga isolated o pulu-pulong mga pag-ulan, pagkidlat at pagkulog,” he added.
(Most of Mindanao, meanwhile, can expect fair weather, although isolated rain showers and thunderstorms are also still possible.)
Pagasa did not raise any gale warnings over the country’s seaboards, Badrina further noted. /jpv

articles.title: [OPINION] Will Pax Silica be another proverbial fish that got away for the Philippines?
articles.summary: Pax Silica cannot be treated as a leisurely long-term development masterplan. It must lock in binding corporate commitments, sign multilateral joint ventures, and physically break ground while it…

blocks.text: It was about six months ago when President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. signed for the country’s participation as the 13th signatory and key player in the US Pax Silica initiative. But nothing concrete seems to have been accomplished more than just that since then.

Beside from drawing immediate opposition from self-styled nationalists, environmental activists and security experts, the government agencies that are supposedly involved in the program seem to be not in synch, much less organized, as to what they should be doing to make things happen — an awkward situation that became glaringly evident from a legislative inquiry made on the matter. This situation could also well explain why the general public is now even more confused than enlightened as to what exactly it is all about, what are at stake, and what is in it for the country to be a key player.

It also appears that this lack of coordination among the government agencies involved in the international initiative and coalition framework appears to be contributing more to the confusion of the general public than the disinformation campaign sowed against Pax Silica by the vociferous individuals and interest groups regarded as nothing but China’s puppies by the silent majority who actually form the true backbone of the country.

As I see it, the longer the government stays this way, there is a good chance that Pax Silica may again become the proverbial fish that got away. To quote the popular local idiom that best captures its regrettable outcome in vivid and derisive terms, “’Pag hindi tayo kumilos agad, maiiwan na naman tayo sa pancitan dito.” (In plain English, ‘If we don’t act fast enough, we will miss out on this, again.’)

To truly understand the real issues and opportunities it brings, the Monday Circle forum dedicated its bimonthly meeting last August 24 — in the way it has always been designed as a platform — to distill and breakdown issues like this high-level multilateral structural blueprint for collaboration into its coherent concept. Two very qualified and independent-minded consultants, very updated on the subject, were invited as resource persons to steer the discussions, namely: Claire Tayco and Cesar Tolentino.

Claire Tayco is the CEO of Cirrolytix Research Services, a research and advancement firm working at the intersection of data, artificial intelligence, public policy, and social impact. She is a statistician and data scientist by training, and spent much of her career in quantitative risk management before moving into AI, analytics, governance, and policy work.

Her recent works through Cirrolytix revolve around how emerging technologies like AI is reshaping economies and geopolitics, and where should the Philippines position itself — similar to the question on Pax Silica.

Cesar Tolentino is a statistician by training with more or less three decades of consulting experience providing strategic advice in today’s many top BPO industry firms. His stint with the University of Asia and the Pacific and consulting company XMG Asia-Pacific, led him to expand his practice into IT and telecom, supporting the growth plans of companies in the industry. To name a few, these included Broadband Philippines, Converge ICT, Microsoft Philippines, Oracle Philippines, and PLDT. He serviced as well entities like the American Chamber of Commerce of the Philippines (AmCham), Asian Development Bank (ADB), IT and Business Process Association of the Philippines (IBPAP), Philippine Chamber of Commerce and Industry (PCCI), US Agency for International Development (USAID), the World Bank, and an extensive consulting work with the members of the Semiconductors and Electronics Industries in the Philippines Inc. (SEIPI).

blocks.caption: [ANALYSIS] Semiconductor industry expected to outperform due to investment surge

blocks.text: This shift also gave him the opportunity to work for the Congressional Committee for Science Technology and Engineering (COMSTE), providing research support for the creation of various legislations such as the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012, the Design Competitiveness Act of 2013 and the DICT Act of 2015. With such exposure, he continues to provide legislative support and assistance in the areas of industry development and capacity-building for the Business Process Outsourcing (BPO), creative industries, energy/power, healthcare, and telecommunication sectors.

Finally, he has contributed to various government development initiatives for such organizations as the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR), Department of Trade and Industry (DTI), Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA), Department of Agriculture (DA), Board of Investments (BOI), Center for International Trade Expositions and Missions (CITEM), Design Center of the Philippines (DCP), Department of Energy (DOE), Department of Science and Technology (DOST), Department of Finance (DOF), Philippine Economic Zone Authority (PEZA), and the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS).

Tolentino gave a good historical overview behind the US Pax Silica initiative which could be traced back to the COVID-19 crisis of 2020 when, as a result, “the US experienced an economic shutdown caused by global supply chain disruptions” together with “China’s growing role as the world’s factory.”

Considering their balance of trade dispute, Tolentino said the US sought for ways to mitigate its economy’s susceptibility to another supply chain shutdown should their dispute with China escalate. The US assembled a coalition of allies for building a strategic supply chain that would decouple and gain strategic autonomy from China.

As part of its strategy to retain US global dominance in AI technological expertise and leadership which is its most important economic product, the US also devised this plan to “redefine the policy framework of its economic relationship with China — a country that is dependent on US technological expertise in AI but at the same time the country that is also seeking global leadership in the same technology.”

Pax Silica, therefore, is clearly an American initiative to primarily advance American interests and global technological dominance. Also, the program brings several concerns that may pose as a problem to the host country such as the Philippines.

On December 11, 2025, the US announced the Pax Silica Summit and the planned signing of the Pax Silica Declaration to serve as the US State Department’s flagship effort on AI and supply-chain security. The Philippines was invited to join the alliance after the December 2025 Summit, in which it did eventually on April 17, 2026.

The US described Pax Silica as a framework focused on securing supply chains for advanced technologies such as semiconductors, artificial intelligence (AI) and rare earth elements. The initiative also implicitly targets reducing reliance on China and countering its dominance in these fields.

For the Philippines, this will involve the development of a 4,000-acre (roughly, 1,619 hectares) “economic security zone” into an “AI-native industrial hub,” purposely built for advanced manufacturing and semiconductor operations in New Clark City (in Capas, Tarlac), a planned community project envisioned by the Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) in 2012 as a proposed new capital city in lieu of Metro Manila.

blocks.caption: PAX SILICA. US Undersecretary for Economic Affairs Jacob Helberg (center) and BCDA CEO Joshua Bingcang (right) and World Bank Deputy Valerie Levkov (second from right) at the unveiling of the marker for Pax Silica at the site of the Economic Security Zone in New Clark City on May 18, 2026.

blocks.text: Out of the total area earmarked for the project, 40% (648 hectares) is to be set aside “exclusively for open spaces, parks, and green zones. BCDA is to further deploy a surface water harvesting system to store rainwater rather than extract groundwater. This initial facility will supply up to 120 million liters per day — a volume well above the project’s estimated daily demand of 65 to 90 million liters — that may offer a potential surplus water to nearby local communities.
All of the project’s components will secure Environmental Compliance Certificates (ECCs) and adhere to strict oversight from the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR).

The project is not to displace indigenous communities so much so that Pax Silica will be located within the public land titled to BCDA under its 1992 Charter. The indigenous communities living in Bamban, Porac, and Floridablanca have over 15,000 hectares dedicated for them in the Clark Special Economic Zone.

blocks.caption: Pax Silica: BCDA’s claims and the counterarguments

blocks.text: Pax Silica is also supposedly to be a purely commercial initiative and will not host defense-related activities or on-site mining operations but would consume 3 gigawatts of electricity at full capacity. According to BCDA, the power will be mostly supplied by embedded power plants installed inside New Clark City, composed of solar and LNG sources. (READ: Why Energy Secretary Garin says Pax Silica is ‘too dangerous’ to plug into grid)

The industries to be hosted are infrastructure, renewable energy power production, surface water harvesting system with water recycling facilities, digital communication infrastructure, logistics infrastructure connecting New Clark City to Clark International Airport and Subic, AI-native manufacturing supply chain, critical mineral processing, semiconductor manufacturing, manufacturing for automotive and consumer electronics, and AI data centers.

Tayco aptly provided the proper perspective on the state of the project and how to shift through the various issues attached to it. What became clear is that the government agencies involved in the project still have to show concrete project plans tying up the key components of the planned industries seamlessly as it should in resolving all the contentious problems.

To reiterate, the government agencies still have no demonstrable proof of viability on the vital issues concerning the implementation of the planned project. They have yet to give proof that the indigenous peoples in the surrounding areas will not be impacted but would actually benefit economically from Pax Silica. They still have to show proof of the sustainability of the water management program claimed together with the evidence that the embedded power system will not impact the supply and price of electricity in the surrounding areas. Finally, the government agencies tasked for the project still have no demonstrable proof showing the economic benefits to be generated by the industries that will be located in the Pax Silica property. (READ: [The Wide Shot] Why Pax Silica concerns people of faith)
In other words, the government has so far not made conclusive steps to warrant the start of the project.

blocks.caption: Pax Silica not in proposed 2027 budget as economic managers say nothing final yet

blocks.text: First and foremost, Pax Silica gives the Philippines a historic opportunity to transcend its legacy role as a low-margin microchip testing outpost and establish itself as a front-end technology sovereign. Due to its strategic geography and geopolitical alignment, too, Pax Silica was handed down to the Philippines with all the opportunities that it could offer to secure its economic future.

These were recognized in the President’s 2026 State of the Nation Address when he mentioned that Pax Silica comes with various economic benefits, foremost of which is “the generation of quality jobs to the people, accelerating the country’s industrial competitiveness, and revitalizing the Philippine economy.” Pax Silica was also recognized as a strategic component of the Luzon Economic Development program which was forged as the multilateral infrastructure and economic development project connecting the key economic growth centers of Subic Bay, Clark, Metro Manila, and Batangas.

Likewise, Pax Silica is seen as a means of reducing the country’s dependence on China with whom the Philippines continues to have contentious relations with regard to maritime claims and territorial sovereignty in the South China Sea — a situation that is anticipated to escalate further in the future and imperil the Philippines’ economic growth and stability.

In the meantime, across Southeast Asia, a frantic grab for this opportunity is already occurring: Malaysia is leveraging its pre-existing ecosystem in Penang, backed by a US$5.3 billion state fund, to transition into advanced logic chip design. Vietnam is weaponizing 37-year preferential tax rates and absorbing land fees to capture hyper-scale factories. Simultaneously, Thailand’s Siam Silica program is deploying a unified, single-board regulatory framework alongside a 200-billion-baht subsidy pool to build a domestic semiconductor foundation by 2030.

The Philippines’ current geopolitical leverage is also subject to rapid obsolescence in the face of shifting economic and geopolitical conditions. Pax Silica cannot be treated as a leisurely long-term development masterplan. It must lock in binding corporate commitments, sign multilateral joint ventures, and physically break ground while it possesses maximum geopolitical value to its Western allies.

As Tolentino recalls, he was then a senior researcher for the Congressional Commission on Science, Technology, and Engineering (COMSTE) when the Philippines, with its bureaucratic pace and policy choice, was left behind by Taiwan in the global chip race in 2009.

As the title of this column says, with the government’s slow pace and indecisiveness, there is a clear and present danger that “Pax Silica could be again the proverbial fish that got away if the Philippines does not get its act together soon.” – Rappler.com
A veteran stocks columnist, Den Somera is a licensed stockbroker and founder of the Monday Circle Financial Forum. You may reach him at densomera@yahoo.com

articles.title: LPA east of Luzon develops into tropical depression, stays out of PAR
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — A low pressure area (LPA) east of Luzon developed into a tropical depression but was unlikely to enter the Philippine area of responsibility (PAR), the Philippine Atmospheric,…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — A low pressure area (LPA) east of Luzon developed into a tropical depression but was unlikely to enter the Philippine area of responsibility (PAR), the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) said on Friday.

In the agency’s 5 a.m. forecast, Pagasa weather specialist Obet Badrina noted that the tropical depression, formerly designated as LPA 09a, was last located 1,700 kilometers east of extreme northern Luzon as of 3 a.m.
“Base naman sa ating pinakahuling update, posible na itong tropical depression ay medyo maliit yung posibilidad na pumasok ng Philippine area of responsibility,” Badrina explained.
(Based on our latest update, this tropical depression may have a low chance of entering the Philippine area of responsibility.)

“Ang pinapakita ng mga datos natin, posible ito na humina at magiging isang low pressure area na lang at maging bahagi ng Bagyong Pilandok (international name: Krovanh) na ngayong ay patungo na sa southern part ng Japan,” he added.
(What our data shows is that it will possibly weaken and turn into a low pressure area and merge with Cyclone Pilandok, which is now heading to the southern part of Japan.)
Krovanh left the PAR on Thursday morning.
However, in a tropical cyclone outlook bulletin at 4 a.m. on Friday, Pagasa said Krovanh was still monitoring the possibility that it would re-enter the agency’s monitoring domain in the coming days.

The state weather bureau added that Tropical Depression Saudel (formerly known by the local name Obet) had weakened into an LPA and was “unlikely to redevelop into a tropical depression within the next 24 hours.”
Badrina noted that no other LPAs nor tropical cyclones had been monitored inside PAR as of Friday morning. /jpv

articles.title: Judge rules 2,000 Catalina Island deer can be killed to save native plant species
articles.summary:
Cull of animals that eat native shrubs, causing spread of fast-igniting grasses, to go ahead despite fierce opposition

Locals and tourists have long fawned over Catalina Island’s mule deer…

blocks.text: Locals and tourists have long fawned over Catalina Island’s mule deer population. For nearly a century, the ungulates have roamed the land’s waterfronts and woodlands, so comfortable around humans that it is not uncommon to spot deer roaming downtown Avalon.
But that sight will soon disappear, after a judge this week paved the way for the island’s conservancy to kill nearly all the island’s 2,000 deer.

A non-profit controlling 88% of the island off the southern California coast has been trying for years to eliminate a non-native deer population. Experts statewide have expressed support for the Catalina Island Conservancy proposal, saying the deer’s consumption of a native shrub plant has led to a growth of an invasive grass species that ignites faster and spreads fire more easily.

The prospect of killing so many deer has sparked fierce – and emotional – opposition from the public, creating an unlikely coalition of animal activists and hunters that has tried to prevent the culling in court. An online petition against the move has garnered more than 32,000 signatures.

Los Angeles county supervisor Janice Hahn, an outspoken critic of the deer’s killing, asked California’s governor, Gavin Newsom, to intervene earlier this week. But the plea was to no avail, and on Thursday a county judge issued a final ruling denying a preliminary injunction filed by opponents.

The conservancy said it would now move forward with a five-year plan to eliminate the island’s deer population, according to its director of communications, Pepe Barton, with an estimated 200 to be hunted with rifles over the next two months. Formally known as Santa Catalina Island, it is the last leg of the Channel Islands to remove non-native deer species.
Barton said the conservancy’s decision was “never our first choice”.

“We understand the gravity of the situation and the responsibility, and it’s a noble sacrifice on the part of the deer that didn’t ask for this,” Barton said. “But this is a necessary step to protect the island, the native plants and animals that are only found here, as well as the residents and livelihoods that depend on Catalina.”

Hunters first introduced mule deer to Catalina for sport about a century ago. What began as a population of a few quickly grew to a few thousand, and save for minor dips in drought seasons, the island’s deer population has not dwindled.

The animals developed an appetite for shrubs native to the island. That presented a unique ecological problem, according to Anna L Jacobsen, a professor and plant biologist at California State University, Bakersfield, who studied the island deer’s relationship with its vegetation after its last major fires in 2006 and 2007.

Jacobsen said when non-native deer eat shrubs already threatened by climate change, the native plants cannot regenerate or recover fast enough, and can become locally extinct. They are subsequently replaced by invasive grasses that ignite and spread fire faster than native species.

In southern California, which has seen increasingly dangerous wildfire seasons in recent years, prevention “has shifted away from, say, fuel reduction to focusing on ignitions”, according to Max Moritz, a wildfire specialist who provides scientific advisory to California state and local governments.
Seeing that loss, and increasingly concerned as wildfires become more frequent across California, scientists sought deer population control measures.

The conservancy examined contraception and sterilization for the deer, which Barton said was infeasible for such a large population. They considered fencing the animals, but it “just isn’t a thing that would be approved”, he said. Four decades of regular hunting seasons have not been enough to reduce populations. And introducing new predators would create new risks to native animals and local people, Barton said.
That leaves total extermination. The conservancy filed for a restoration management permit with the California department of fish and wildlife, which in January approved the plan.

Only a small population of deer will be sterilized – those living near the town of Avalon – and all others will be killed. Island residents will be allowed one last hunting season from late October to mid-December of this year.

The meat from the deer killing will go to the California condor recovery program or local tribal groups, and Barton said deer carcasses near trails or roads will be removed; only those in steep, dangerous terrain will be allowed to decompose naturally. People traveling or hiking the island will not regularly see deer carcasses, Barton said.

Still, the question over what to do about Catalina’s deer has created a complex situation where “people feel some strong attachment to the deer” and it becomes difficult to see the science behind decisions, Moritz said. “But the fact is, you can’t realistically constrain the deer to graze only targeted areas ... From a scientific, ecological, and fire perspective, removal is the best way.”

articles.title: Eala earns swift US Open win vs Oliynykova to reach 3rd round

items: Alex Eala advanced to the third round of the US Open with a 6-1, 6-4 victory over Oleksandra Oliynykova, marking a significant improvement from her previous year's performance.
Eala showcased her skills by dominating the match, winning the first set in just 23 minutes and maintaining a strong lead throughout, ultimately finishing the match in 1 hour and 3 minutes.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – Alex Eala has come so far that a win in a Grand Slam no longer feels like a surprise.

The Filipina tennis star rolled into the third round of the US Open following a masterful 6-1, 6-4 victory over Ukraine’s Oleksandra Oliynykova at the Louis Armstrong Stadium in Flushing Meadows, New York, on Thursday, September 3 (Friday, September 4, Manila time).

A scorching start set the tone for the swift triumph as Eala surpassed her finish in the same tournament last year, when she stunned Denmark’s Clara Tauson to become the first Filipino to win a Grand Slam main draw match in the Open Era, before she fell to Spain’s Cristina Bucsa in the second round.
“I think my patience and the consistency of my focus — I think those were the key to winning the match today,” said Eala.
Matching her lofty billing as the 17th seed, Eala won the first nine points en route to 4-0 lead before she clinched the opening set in just 23 minutes.

Oliynykova, ranked 46th in the world, refused to go down without a fight, grabbing a 2-1 lead in the second set and battling back to level at 3-3 before Eala closed out the match by winning three of the final four games.
Eala sealed the win with a serve that forced an errant return from Oliynykova as she concluded the match in just 1 hour and 3 minutes for one of her fastest victories in a Grand Slam.

Fueled by the support of flag-waving Filipinos, Eala dominated Oliynykova throughout, firing 13 more winners (19-6) and committing 12 fewer errors (12-24) on the way to a 59-35 advantage in total points.
“I think we all represent something and I’m proud of what I represent,” said Eala.

The win allowed Eala to get back at Oliynykova just four months after she lost to the Ukrainian in their maiden WTA Tour encounter, absorbing a three-set loss in the opening round of the Strasbourg Open in France in May.
Eala has yet to drop a set in this US Open as she also swept USA’s Mary Stoiana, 6-1, 6-2, to begin her campaign.
Up next for Eala in the round of 32 is the winner between American world No. 14 Iva Jovic and British world No. 104 Francesca Jones. – Rappler.com

articles.title: High-profile VPD officer and youth charity CEO Kal Dosanjh charged with theft, fraud
articles.summary: Vancouver police officer, anti-gang advocate and youth charity CEO Kal Dosanjh has been charged with theft, fraud and breach of trust offences dating back to 2017.

image.caption: A file photo of Vancouver Police officer Kal Dosanjh in 2018. He has been charged with multiple instances of fraud over $5,000. (Doug Kerr/CBC)

blocks.text: British Columbia·Updated
Vancouver police officer, anti-gang advocate and youth charity CEO Kal Dosanjh has been charged with theft, fraud and breach of trust offences dating back to 2017.
Alleged offences go back as far as 2017
Dosanjh was arrested and taken into custody on Thursday.
A charge document reveals he is facing multiple counts of fraud over $5,000, and theft over $5,000.
According to the document sworn on Thursday, multiple charges relate to alleged fraud and stealing from investors of multiple property development projects.
Those include the Azura, Queen's Park and Sahara development projects.
The alleged offences occurred between Jan. 13, 2017, and Oct. 31, 2024, according to the document, with Sarabjit Singh Gill listed as a co-defendant.
According to B.C. Supreme Court documents, the two men are listed as partners in multiple property development ventures, which have been the subject of multiple civil lawsuits.
The two have denied all wrongdoing in those cases.
Dosanjh also faces two charges alleging he committed fraud over $5,000 and stole from the KidsPlay Youth Foundation, the charity that he founded in 2015.
Those alleged crimes occurred between Dec. 8, 2017, and July 25, 2025, according to the document.
Dosanjh also faces one count of breach of trust by a public officer.
On Thursday afternoon, plain-clothes and uniformed VPD officers were seen carrying boxes out of a home listed as Dosanjh's residence in court documents.
Dosanjh has been a VPD employee for more than two decades.
In 2015, he founded the KidsPlay Youth Foundation, a charity with the stated aim of "keeping B.C. kids away from a life of crime."
Dosanjh has made multiple media appearances in his role as the charity's CEO, with the non-profit often organizing sports events in a bid to engage youth with community programs.

items: Vancouver police officer charged with 1 count of assault

blocks.text: Alliance Lawyers in Langley, a law firm representing Dosanjh, sent CBC News a statement saying it was "inappropriate to draw conclusions" based on the reported arrest of their client.
"Mr. Dosanjh has committed no crime and is innocent of any wrongdoing," the statement reads.
"An arrest, or a report that an arrest has occurred, is not evidence of guilt, misconduct, or criminal responsibility."

articles.title: Mindoro’s rarest bird captured on camera after nearly two decades
articles.summary: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — A critically endangered bird that’s considered one of Mindoro’s rarest species has been captured on camera for the first time in nearly two decades, offering…

blocks.text: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — A critically endangered bird that’s considered one of Mindoro’s rarest species has been captured on camera for the first time in nearly two decades, offering conservationists fresh hope for its survival in the island’s remaining forests.

The Mindoro bleeding-heart (Gallicolumba platenae) was photographed in August at an elevation of more than 900 meters within the Iraya Mangyan ancestral domain, according to the Center for Conservation Innovation Philippines Inc. (CCIPH).

The sighting was made through an indigenous Filipino-led conservation initiative involving Iraya Mangyan communities and CCIPH under the Mindoro Forest and Biodiversity Conservation Programme (MFBCP).
The latest record is particularly significant because the species has remained largely unseen for about 20 years, according to the conservation group.
The bird was documented at an elevation higher than locations where it had historically been recorded, providing potentially important information on its remaining habitat and distribution.

The Mindoro bleeding-heart is endemic to Mindoro and is among the Philippines’ most threatened birds. Its survival is closely tied to the protection of the island’s remaining forest habitats, which face continuing pressures from habitat loss and degradation.
For conservationists, the photograph represents more than a rare wildlife record.

It provides evidence that the species may still persist in relatively intact portions of Mindoro’s forests and highlights the importance of protecting these areas, particularly within indigenous Filipino ancestral domains.
The involvement of Iraya Mangyan communities also underscores their role in safeguarding Mindoro’s biodiversity. /jpv

articles.title: Mimaropa police strengthen efforts to detect youth radicalization
articles.summary: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — The Police Regional Office in Mimaropa is bolstering its capability to detect and address early warning signs of violence and radicalization among the youth by…

blocks.text: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — The Police Regional Office in Mimaropa is bolstering its capability to detect and address early warning signs of violence and radicalization among the youth by holding a three-day seminar-workshop on Nihilistic Violent Extremism (NVE), which ends on Friday (September 4).

The seminar brought together police personnel from Occidental and Oriental Mindoro, Marinduque, Romblon, and Palawan, alongside officials from the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) in response to recent nationwide incidents of violence involving children and adolescents, as well as concerns over harmful online content and other factors that may expose young people to radicalization and risk.
Participants were taught to recognize behavioral and digital indicators, understand the drivers of radicalization, assess threats, and apply proper intervention and referral mechanisms.
The seminar also covers local threat environments, emerging case patterns, and the need for coordinated action among police officers, social workers, schools, families, and local governments.

Col. Hordan T. Pacatiatiw, Deputy Regional Director for Operations, emphasized that incidents outside Mimaropa should serve as a call to strengthen local preparedness “before a similar situation occurs in our communities.”
The training also underscores the need for child-sensitive interventions that prioritize the welfare, age, and circumstances of minors, including their protection and rehabilitation.
Brigadier Gen. Christopher R. Dela Cruz, Mimaropa police regional director, stressed the importance of acting early rather than waiting for tragedy.

“We should not wait for a tragedy before we start asking questions. If there are risks we can recognize today, then we have a responsibility to understand them and act before they cause harm,” Dela Cruz said.

“When a child is at risk, the police cannot be the only answer. We need families, schools, social workers, local governments, and communities to recognize what is happening and help before the situation gets worse,” he emphasized in a statement. /jpv

articles.title: Venezuelans of all stripes are denouncing Trump's 'biggest oil deal ever'
articles.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump's oil deal with interim Venezuelan President Delcy Rodriguez is being rejected by the Venezuelan opposition, and by some in her own party. Venezuelan Canadians, some with…

image.caption: U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright and Venezuelan interim President Delcy Rodriguez shake hands at Miraflores Palace in Caracas, Venezuela, on Wednesday. (Leonardo Fernandez Viloria/Reuters)

blocks.text: Venezuela's opposition leader Maria Corina Machado broke several days of silence on Thursday with a video statement in which she rejected the oil deal signed on Wednesday in Caracas between the U.S. government and Venezuela's interim president, Delcy Rodriguez.

"I understand what you are feeling," she told her compatriots, "sadness, anger and that painful feeling so familiar throughout our history of someone else making decisions about what belongs to us, in our name, without asking us."
Machado's statement came a day after both Trump and Rodriguez refused to offer any schedule for a return to democracy in Venezuela, and Trump again praised the Rodriguez government.
"We are very happy with the president-elect that we have right now, the people that are running it," Trump said on Tuesday. (Rodriguez has not, in fact, been elected to the post.)
Trump announces deal to control vast amount of Venezuelan oil reserves

While she had always believed Venezuela's oil industry needed U.S. investment to recover, Machado said, Rodriguez's government had no legitimacy to make such a deal, which needed to wait for the return of democracy and rule of law.
She also said there was confusion about the real terms of the deal. Many Venezuelans share that confusion, but already know they don't like it.

Neither U.S. President Donald Trump and U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio's social media posts, nor a White House statement, nor Rodriguez's speech clarified exactly how or when 17 Venezuelan oilfields would be rejuvenated and start producing the 65 billion barrels covered by Trump's "biggest oil deal ever."
Extracting oil over releasing prisoners
Many Venezuelan Canadians, including some with deep knowledge of the country's oil industry, have reacted negatively to the announcement.

"It's frustration, disappointment and rage," said Rebecca Sarfatti of Toronto, co-founder of the Canada Venezuela Democracy Forum. "We were used as a country, as an oil power, to get whatever Trump wanted. And Miss Delcy is playing the game so she can stay in power."
Sarfatti says Venezuelans are exasperated by the eagerness to get at Venezuela's resources and the relative lack of interest in liberating political prisoners.

Lino Carrillo, former general manager of operations for Nexen Energy in Fort McMurray, Alta., and a veteran of both Venezuela's and Canada's oil industries, is a member of Machado's advisory group on oil and energy.

"Anybody that signs with Delcy will be exposed to transparency in the end," he told CBC News. "When a new government comes in, they're going to review everything that has been signed by Delcy, by Trump or any U.S. government, or any European government for that matter."
"What they're doing is against the constitution of Venezuela."

Venezuelans have grown increasingly skeptical of U.S. motivations in their country since the Jan. 3 capture of Nicolas Maduro, he said: "There is an old saying that you judge people for what they do and not for what they say."

The announcement by Trump only sharpened Venezuelans' frustration at the fact that eight months after the U.S. seized Maduro in the raid on Caracas, the dictatorship he led has been allowed to remain in power, while Trump describes its unelected leader as "highly respected."

Among Republican politicians in Florida, there were growing signs of unease with the closeness of the Trump administration to the rump chavista dictatorship that has become its partner in Venezuela. Florida Republicans complained about the lack of movement toward democracy and expressed support for Machado, repeatedly scorned by the Trump administration.

The deal also appeared to split Delcy Rodriguez's own party. Prominent chavista congresswoman Iris Varela put out a video statement saying the deal was signed "under duress" and vowing to repudiate it as soon as Trump leaves office.
Even some of the most enthusiastic "MAGAzuelans," the Venezuelans who most put their trust in Trump and criticized anyone who disagreed, appeared to be rethinking their assessments.
Controversial figure at the centre of the deal

Venezuelan criticisms of the deal focus on the fact that it was negotiated secretly with an illegitimate government, through a Venezuelan intermediary seen in the country as a classic example of the bolichico class — a businessman who has profited through his connections to the chavista regime.
A fact sheet published by the White House on Monday night described an unusual joint venture between the Pentagon and a private company called North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP).

items: Trump's Venezuelan oil deal: What we know and how it could impact Canada's oil industry
The U.S. could soon control 20% of Venezuela's oil reserves. Canada's oilpatch isn't worried
Chevron expands Venezuela presence with $7B US plan

blocks.text: The U.S. State Department would have a right to 20 per cent of production "at cost," and right of first refusal on the remaining 80 per cent. Venezuela would be guaranteed $19 US per barrel in royalties, regardless of the price of oil.

NABEP was formed out of Blue Energy, a company run by Florida oil and asphalt magnate Harry Sargeant III, a Trump golf partner and major GOP donor who did a lot of business with the Maduro regime (Maduro once called him "the only gringo I trust.")
But Sargeant sold his stake to Venezuelan businessman Alejandro Betancourt, who has been investigated for allegedly laundering embezzled Venezuelan money in several countries, but never charged.
Rubio defended Betancourt's involvement by saying he is not suspected of wrongdoing on U.S. territory, as U.S. media reported Trump administration pressure campaigns to drop European investigations.
A 'highly irregular' deal
Venezuelan Canadians in the oil industry have no illusions about the state of the industry they were forced to leave behind.
Jorge Robles, who spent his career in Venezuelan and Albertan oilfields, says people understand that Venezuela needs foreign investment and that it has to give something in return.
"I was prepared to have negotiations that were very uncomfortable and disadvantageous to Venezuela," he told CBC News.
But he said there was something "highly irregular" about the way this deal was negotiated.
"The U.S. is there negotiating on behalf of the Venezuelan reserve, but to offer that to companies that belong to the United States. So it's an obvious conflict of interest," he said.
Robles said it was "really upsetting and concerning" that the administration is focusing on oil, rather than political prisoners.
He said he fears that any money Venezuela receives will merely be used by the chavista regime to further entrench itself.
Midterm voters may be true target

But the two oilmen also say that given the deal's cold reception in Venezuela, oil companies are unlikely to want to bet on its long-term survival, or on a country where the situation remains so uncertain.

"If we don't get to a situation where there is a due process in Venezuela, freedom and people can walk on the street without fear, then don't expect any company to send people to Venezuela," said Robles.
They both said the announced deal appeared to be partly about convincing American voters in the run-up to the midterms that high gas prices will soon start dropping.
What could massive U.S. and Venezuelan oil deal mean for Alberta?

"It's just a lot of noise to try to influence votes in the States," said Carrillo, adding that the price of oil will respond far more to any reopening in the Strait of Hormuz than far-off plans for oil investment in the Orinoco Basin.
"The markets are not dumb," he said. "The markets are watching that."

Carrillo said he intends to return to Venezuela to offer his expertise to put the devastated oil industry back on its feet, but won't do so unless there is a deal ratified by a democratic Venezuelan government.
Fears of creeping colonization

Many Venezuelans have expressed fears of a creeping colonization of their country, in which the chavista dictatorship is maintained in power by the Trump administration as a subcontractor of its control.

"I do feel it's kind of happening in a very kind of smooth way," said Sarfatti. "And probably the earthquake is helping that to happen more just because we do need help, but not necessarily from a colonizing country."

The guardianship the White House has claimed over Venezuela, she said, "is definitely a level of taking over. You can see that when Venezuelan leaders who've been working for 20-something years to recover our country are just set aside."

items: Smith sees no threat to Alberta from U.S.-Venezuela oil deal, renews pipeline push
Federal government will extend gas tax holiday into 2027

blocks.text: The fear now for the Venezuelan opposition is that the Americans' lucrative deal with Rodriguez only gives Washington additional motives to keep her dictatorship in place.
Likewise the U.S. has little motive to demand the release of political prisoners who might challenge the legitimacy of the deal or the government that signed it.
"They were talking about releasing political prisoners, about freedom of press," Sarfatti said. "but then time passed by and Trump's true colours came out.
"We never expected from a country like the U.S., who has been the lead of democracy for so long, to behave the way it's behaving."

articles.title: Missouri supreme court throws out new congressional maps backed by Trump
articles.summary:
Setback for Republicans in redistricting battle as court orders forbids maps from being used in November elections

The Missouri supreme court has unanimously blocked new congressional…

blocks.text: The Missouri supreme court has unanimously blocked new congressional districts backed by Donald Trump from being used in the November election and ordered a statewide vote on whether to uphold or reject the new map.

The decision Thursday marks a rare setback for Republicans in a national redistricting battle. Republicans had hoped Missouri’s new congressional boundaries could help them win an additional seat and hold onto their slim House majority in the midterms. The ruling still could be appealed to the US supreme court.

Missouri’s new districts were used in the August primaries. But the state supreme court said they cannot be used in the November general election – or ever again, unless voters first uphold the new districts passed by the Republican-led legislature.
The court placed the new districts on hold because citizens submitted petition signatures seeking a referendum.

“The referendum petition was legal, sufficient, and timely, and the secretary incorrectly concluded otherwise,” the court said in its ruling. The legislation containing the new districts “did not go into effect and will not go into effect unless and until approved by the voters.” As as result, the congressional map adopted after the 2020 census “remains in full force and effect for the November 2026 general election”.

The Missouri constitution does not specifically say a referendum petition can be used for a congressional redistricting law passed by the legislature. But the supreme court ruled that a constitutional provision allowing a referendum on “any act” of the Legislature encompasses congressional redistricting.
The ruling capped a year of political maneuvering and legal wrangling over the new districts.

After Trump urged Republicans to redraw congressional districts to their advantage, Missouri governor Mike Kehoe called lawmakers into a special session last year to dramatically reconfigure the fifth congressional district, held by Democrat Emanuel Cleaver.

Opponents submitted over 300,000 petition signatures in December seeking to put the map to a vote of the people. But Republican secretary of state Denny Hoskins waited until primary election day in August to reject the petition. He asserted that the referendum process cannot be used for congressional redistricting. A lower court agreed , resulting in an appeal to the state’s highest court, which overturned Hoskins’ decision.
Attorneys representing Hoskins and Republican party committees had argued it was too close to the general election to revert to the prior districts without causing confusion and chaos.
Missouri currently has six Republicans and two Democrats in the US House.
Cleaver, who was unopposed in the August primary, has carried the Kansas City-based district with at least 60% of the vote in each of the past two elections.

Republican state senator Rick Brattin won an August primary in the reshaped fifth congressional district, which had been stretched eastward to include rural Republican areas. About 59% of the district’s voters were new under the revised map, according to an Associated Press estimate.

Cleaver had not posted campaign signs in many of the new rural areas, explaining that he was waiting for the Missouri supreme court’s decision. But he had vowed to continue his re-election campaign regardless of the outcome.

Congressional districts typically are redrawn at the start of each decade, based on new census data. But Trump’s quest for a midterm election advantage triggered an unusual mid-decade redistricting battle that spread to more than a dozen states — and triggered a dozen lawsuits in Missouri alone. All told, Republicans had hoped to net as many as 10 additional seats nationally.
The Missouri supreme court ruling was one of only a few nationally to go against Republicans’ redistricting plans.
Prior to its latest ruling, Missouri’s top court already had rejected claims that the special session was illegal, mid-decade redistricting isn’t allowed and the new districts aren’t compact enough .

articles.title: FIFA blames UEFA for 'smear campaign' against Infantino
articles.summary: The dispute between the two football associations reached a US court, in which UEFA is looking for permission to collect evidence for criminal proceedings in Switzerland.

image.caption: UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin (left) and FIFA President Gianni Infantino have been at odds [FILE: June 2024]Image: Nick Potts/PA Images/IMAGO

blocks.text: World football governing body FIFA took a lash at Europe's UEFA for starting a "smear campaign" and "fishing expedition" against FIFA and its President Gianni Infantino.

This comes after a dispute between the two organizations due to FIFA's plan to sell a stake in its commercial rights, with UEFA submitting an ex parte application to the US District Court in New York to obtain testimony and documents from US-based entities. These documents will be used in potential criminal proceedings in Switzerland, where both FIFA and UEFA are based.
Such criminal proceedings are currently being considered, UEFA previously said.
In documents seen by Reuters, FIFA called the application "little more than press releases" to support UEFA's "smear campaign against FIFA and its leadership."

blocks.caption: Spain won the 2026 FIFA World Cup [FILE: July 2026]Image: Evrim Aydin/Anadolu/picture alliance

blocks.text: According to UEFA, the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), an entity which would have had the commercial rights linked over the FIFA World Cup to investors was developed without adequate consulting FIFA's 211 member associations, as well as FIFA's own governing bodies.
UEFA threatened to boycott the FIFA World Cup should the move go ahead.
The move would have affected both the men's and the women's tournaments.
FIFA argued that the association representing European football had tried to scupper the proposal with a bid to keep European football's dominance as is.
Demands for Infatino's resignation
Pressure has been mounting on both FIFA and its President Gianni Infantino since the FFE plans were made public.

blocks.caption: Criticism is mounting over FIFA's now-scrapped plans to sell a stake in the World Cup's commercial rights  [FILE: May 2026]Image: Ethan Cairns/ZUMA/IMAGO

blocks.text: This resulted in several countries saying they will not support Infantino's reelection for a fourth term as president in March 2027, when the Swiss-born FIFA boss looks for a fourth term in office.
Aside from UEFA, two other continental confederations demand Infantino's resignation.

Both CONCACAF, representing North and Central America and the Caribbean, and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) voiced their objections to Infantino. Only the South American and African confederations still support him.
UEFA also demanded a "genuinely independent external review" of how the proposal came about.
"FIFA cannot investigate itself and expect the football community to simply accept its conclusions," UEFA said.
FIFA revolt: Can Infantino's Trump connection save him?

articles.title: Transplanted pig kidney works in US man's body for record 271 days
articles.summary: A man has lived for a record nine months with a transplanted pig kidney while waiting for a human transplant.

blocks.text: A kidney transplanted from a pig has worked inside a patient for 271 days – the longest on record, say US doctors.
Tim Andrews said the transplant gave him "hope" and spared him months of needing to go to hospital to have his blood filtered by a dialysis machine.
The team at Mass General Brigham hospital say their work shows pig organs can be used as a "bridge" until a human transplant becomes available.
But the pig organ eventually failed and was removed so Andrews needed a short bout of dialysis before a donor was found.
Doctors and scientists are exploring xenotransplantation – using organs from other species – due to shortages of organs for transplants.
In the US, around 100,000 people are waiting for a kidney while only 25,000 transplants occur each year. More than 7,000 people in the UK are on the kidney transplant list.
Andrews was told it could take seven years to get to the top of the list, but that people live only five years, on average, on dialysis.
"I had a little bit of a shortage of time… it becomes very depressing," he said.
But he described the idea of a pig transplant as "hope" and the "light at the end of the tunnel".
"Hope is the biggest thing, the chance to be free from the [dialysis] machine and live your life."

articles.title: US investigating if missile hit Iran wedding, Vance says
articles.summary: The Iranian Red Crescent Society (IRCS) said shrapnel from a missile hit the ceremony and killed four people on Tuesday.

blocks.text: Watch: JD Vance "extremely sceptical" over alleged strike on Iranian wedding
The US military is investigating Iranian claims that its strikes killed at least four people including two children at a wedding in southern Iran, Vice-President JD Vance has said.
