articles.title: COA flags gaps in confidential fund rules, says multiple SDOs allowed
articles.summary: The Commission on Audit (COA) said it is looking to revisit rules governing confidential and intelligence funds, including the use of aliases, documentation for informants, and the requirements for…

blocks.text: The Commission on Audit (COA) said it is looking to revisit rules governing confidential and intelligence funds, including the use of aliases, documentation for informants, and the requirements for paying rewards, as senators pressed the audit body on safeguards for the disbursement and liquidation of such funds.
During the Senate hearing on COA’s proposed 2027 budget, COA chairperson Gamaliel Cordoba said the existing joint memorandum circular has provisions that need to be reviewed and clarified.

The rules are contained in Joint Circular No. 2015-01, issued by COA, the Department of Budget and Management, the Department of the Interior and Local Government, the Governance Commission for GOCCs and the Department of National Defense. The circular governs the entitlement, release, use, reporting and audit of confidential and intelligence funds.
During the hearing, COA officials clarified that an agency may designate more than one special disbursing officer (SDO) to handle confidential or intelligence funds.

An SDO is responsible for making the disbursements and maintaining the required records for the funds. Under the current rules, cash advances for confidential funds are drawn by duly designated and bonded SDOs or by the head of agency, upon approval of the agency head.
Cordoba said there is no prescribed limit on the number of SDOs an agency may designate.
“Nasa head of agency o ahensya ang pamamaraan kung sino ang assigned SDO,” he said.
(It is up to the head of the agency to determine who will be assigned as SDO.)
The official explained that an agency may have different SDOs for different programs, provided they meet the requirements for accountable officers, including proper bonding and accountability.
“Basta ang SDO can be multiple, there is no limit as long as proper management and proper bonding and accountability can be had,” the official noted.
(There can be multiple SDOs; there is no limit as long as there is proper management, bonding and accountability.)
Under the existing circular, the SDO must maintain separate records of transactions, prepare liquidation and progress reports, and submit the required documents to COA.
COA wants clearer rules on aliases
The discussion also turned to the use of aliases or code names in documents supporting confidential-fund transactions.

He said the existing joint circular does not clearly settle the issue and that COA has identified the use of aliases and the identities appearing in acknowledgment receipts as areas requiring further review.

The concern has also surfaced in recent Senate proceedings, where a former COA auditor testified that Joint Circular No. 2015-01 is silent on whether aliases may be used in documents supporting confidential-fund disbursements.
Cordoba added that the proposed review would look at how identities can be protected without compromising COA’s ability to properly audit the use of public funds.
He said there should be a way for auditors with the appropriate clearance to verify identities where necessary while preserving the confidentiality of intelligence operations and informants.
Proof required for rewards
COA also emphasized that payment for information and payment of rewards are not the same thing.

An official explained that an agency may pay for information as part of a confidential operation, but a reward carries an additional requirement: there must be evidence showing that the information or surveillance activity resulted in a successful outcome.
“Pag-reward ang pinag-usapan natin kakaiba, pag sinabi nating reward may kaakibat na success,” Cordoba noted.
(When we are talking about a reward, it is different; a reward carries with it the requirement of success.)
The official said the rules require documentation showing the success of the information-gathering or surveillance activity.
Possible evidence could include records of an arrest or other documents demonstrating that the information provided led to a concrete result.
“Importante ang dokumento,” the official added.
(The documentation is important.)

The official also added that simply presenting an acknowledgment receipt would not, by itself, establish the success required for a reward. Meanwhile, after two hours of deliberation, the Senate Committee on Finance on Thursday approved the Commission on Audit’s (COA) proposed P16.046-billion budget for 2027.—LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Flood control cases vs Romualdez forthcoming, says Ombudsman Remulla
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Despite the recantation of some potential witnesses, cases related to the flood control anomaly will be filed against former Speaker Martin Romualdez, Ombudsman Jesus Crispin…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Despite the recantation of some potential witnesses, cases related to the flood control anomaly will be filed against former Speaker Martin Romualdez, Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla said Thursday.
“Yes, why not? It’s already there anyway,” Remulla said in Filipino on the sidelines of a Senate finance committee hearing on the proposed budget for the Office of the Ombudsman.
“[The looming cases] are just there. We’re not stopping, and we have not stopped. We have been working hard, and it will come out very soon. You just relax, we’re almost there,” he told reporters.

He said the recantation by some of the former security aides of ex-Ako Bicol Rep. Zaldy Co, including former Marine Orly Guteza, who withdrew his testimony before the Senate that he had delivered suitcases containing millions of pesos in cash to Romualdez’s residence, was merely a “smokescreen” tactic to divert attention from the former House speaker.
“That’s nothing. … That’s only a small part of the case. Of course, that’s being played up by his lawyer,” he said.

Remulla said the Ombudsman is taking a careful approach to ensure it can build and file a strong case against Romualdez, who, he said, has vast resources to manipulate people, including the media, and shield himself from accountability.
“There’s just a lot that really needs to be finished so we can file a strong case… weak cases cannot be filed here. He has a lot of money… a lot of lawyers,” Remulla said.

“As you can see, everyone is on the payroll. There are a lot of lawyers talking, you know that. I will not be surprised if they also attempt to… offer you whatever. I will not be surprised. He has too much money; it’s the people’s money,” he added.

Ade Fajardo, Romualdez’s lawyer and spokesperson, earlier lashed out at the Office of the Ombudsman anew, questioning why the anti-graft body appears to be fixated on his client when there is supposedly no evidence against him. /das

articles.title: DBM chief: Lower-than-requested fund is not a budget cut
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — A lower-than-requested fund allocated to a government agency is not necessarily a budget cut, the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) on Thursday said. The statement came…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — A lower-than-requested fund allocated to a government agency is not necessarily a budget cut, the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) on Thursday said.
The statement came as the Senate began deliberations on the proposed national budget for 2027 amounting to P7.2 trillion.
“Just because the full request wasn’t granted doesn’t mean the budget was cut,” acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert de Leon said during the Alamin kay Sec. Kim program.
De Leon explained that an agency may propose a significantly higher budget for next year, although it is still subject to evaluation.
The DBM would still consider the agencies’ previous budget allocation, utilization, program requirements, available resources, as well as the priorities of the government, he added.
He disclosed that the combined proposals of all government agencies reached approximately P12 trillion, exceeding the P7.2 trillion-ceiling of the proposed national budget.
“The DBM’s job is to ensure that the government’s limited resources go to programs that are truly needed and provide genuine benefits to every Filipino,” he said. /das

articles.title: Ombudsman laments state of judiciary, slow justice system
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla said the judiciary needs to undergo “soul-searching” and be “examined closely by everybody in government” to address long-standing…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla said the judiciary needs to undergo “soul-searching” and be “examined closely by everybody in government” to address long-standing problems in the country’s justice system.
Remulla made the remarks during the Senate committee on finance hearing on Thursday on the proposed 2027 budget of the Office of the Ombudsman.

“It’s just probably unfortunate that I have to mention this. Many of those that we have dismissed in the Office of the Ombudsman institutionally, in many cases, we’re talking about many, many cases, that were reversed by the Court of Appeals,” he said.
“That is a trend that’s known to the whole Office of the Ombudsman,” Remulla said, adding that he had discussed the matter with Supreme Court Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen.

“I told him about this problem that we have because institutionally, it’s very discouraging to be conducting all of these activities only to be reversed by the Court of Appeals decision that came out of nowhere,” he said.
He acknowledged that it was unusual for lawyers to criticize the courts but said the issue needed to be raised.

“As a lawyer, it’s not really common for lawyers to complain about the courts. But sometimes we just have to raise that issue already because it can be the biggest elephant in the room, within our justice system,” the Ombudsman said.
Remulla later told the media that his remarks were prompted by his experience as a lawyer and government official and “something that I have to do for the country.”
“I think my experience as a lawyer and government official and advocate speak for itself, It something that everybody knows but somebody should say it,” he added.

“If there’s one thing that was never touched with all the EDSAs that happened to this country, [it] is the judiciary. Never has the judiciary accounted for everything that they’ve been doing,” he added. “It’s actually a problem that has been there for the longest time, but it has to be said openly.

Meanwhile, Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian urged stronger coordination between the Office of the Ombudsman and the judiciary to make the “wheels of justice” move faster, more efficiently, and more fairly.
He warned that a slow and fragmented justice system undermines accountability, stressing that when cases take years to resolve, it is ultimately the Filipino people who bear the cost.

Gatchalian raised the issue after Remulla told senators that it takes an average of 15 years for the Sandiganbayan to resolve a case. Remulla also said the CA reverses many of the Ombudsman’s decisions.
“I am not blaming them. I am just saying that the wheels of justice are broken. … They seem to be stuck,” Gatchalian said.

He asked what steps the Ombudsman was taking with the judiciary to speed up the resolution of cases, stressing that the Ombudsman’s proactive efforts could be undermined if cases remain stuck in the judicial process.

In response, Remulla said the government could establish a coordinating mechanism involving the Ombudsman and the judiciary, similar to the Justice Sector Coordinating Council he worked with when he was Secretary of Justice.

Such coordination, he said, could help make the “wheels of justice” move faster, noting that delays in resolving cases have long affected not only accountability but also business investments and economic progress.
Gatchalian reiterated his support for efforts to improve the efficiency of the justice system, emphasizing that delays in the accountability process ultimately hurt the public.

“If our accountability mechanisms do not function, from the Ombudsman all the way to the judiciary, it is not necessarily the respondent or the accused who suffers. It is the people who suffer,” Gatchalian said./dp

articles.title: Rise of far-right Vannacci poses dilemma for Meloni as she celebrates Italian milestone
articles.summary: Futuro Nazionale’s speedy rise in polls prompts questions over whether PM will return to her roots before election

blocks.text: Giorgia Meloni’s government has become the longest-running in Italy since the second world war – a milestone the prime minister is determined not to let pass unnoticed.

In the port area of Bari, the capital of the southern Italian region of Puglia, where Meloni hosted the G7 in 2024 and where she spends her summer holiday, preparations are well under way for a festival-style showcase of her rightwing administration.

On Friday, there will be food trucks, water stations and traditional Puglian light shows as part of celebrations to entertain an expected crowd of 10,000 people bussed in from across Italy. Militants from the youth wing of Meloni’s far-right Brothers of Italy party have fanned the city’s squares and beaches for days, handing out flyers promoting the celebrations while wearing T-shirts featuring the official slogan: Il Governo più stabile, l’Italia più forte (the most stable government, the strongest Italy).

Meloni, who just a few weeks ago was booed at the opening ceremony of the Mediterranean Games in Taranto, further south in Puglia, will address the audience in the evening, surrounded by her coalition allies – Matteo Salvini, leader of the far-right League, and conservative Forza Italia’s Antonio Tajani.

“This moment will be written in the history books,” said Michele Picaro, a Brothers of Italy MEP and former Bari councillor. “We are the longest government in the history of the Italian Republic and this must be celebrated.”

blocks.caption: In recent months the political landscape has become less settled for Giorgia Meloni.  Photograph: Francesca Bolla/AGF/Shutterstock

blocks.text: Beneath the triumph, however, the outlook for Meloni is less settled. True, she has enjoyed a political stability that eluded her predecessors. Brothers of Italy is still the country’s biggest party. But in recent months, the political landscape has shifted with the the emergence of a challenger – not from the left or the centre, but from someone who is even further to the right than Meloni.

Since its launch in February, Roberto Vannacci, a former army general, has seen his far-right party, Futuro Nazionale, rise to about 8% in the polls, surpassing his former compatriots in the League months ago and this week eclipsing Forza Italia, too.

Vannacci first entered the public eye in 2023 after self-publishing a book filled with racism, homophobia, Islamophobia and antisemitism. The subsequent backlash cost him his army job, but propelled him to the top of the bestsellers list. Helped along by ample coverage in the Italian press, he capitalised on the notoriety and in 2024 was elected as an MEP for the League, later leaving Salvini’s party to set up his own.

“I read his book because I always think you need to know the enemy,” said Giulia Pastorella, an MP and vice-president of the small centrist party Azione. “And I thought, ‘this is exactly the kind of thing you might hear people talking about in the bar.’ Here’s a military man, who is really a mirror of the worst impulses of people. The scary thing is, I think he’s genuine and not a PR construct.”

His policies, such as they are, are extreme. Futuro Nazionale’s recently published manifesto says that “abortion is not a right” and calls for gay people to be banned from TV between 6am and 11pm so that children aren’t exposed to what it describes as “homosexualist” content. It also proposes introducing military education in high schools and a “remigration” plan to remove irregular immigrants and foreign nationals who commit crimes.

On foreign policy, Vannacci has campaigned to stop weapons and financial aid to Ukraine, saying if he could choose between Vladimir Putin or the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, he would choose Putin.

In July, he organised a “Futuristic Triathlon” in the northern seaside town of Sanremo, billed as an event to “temper the mind and body” in an echo of the fascist aesthetics and themes of the Mussolini era.

blocks.caption: Roberto Vannacci’s policies, such as they are, are extreme. Photograph: Remo Casilli/Reuters

blocks.text: Far from being a treated as a pariah, however, Vannacci’s party has proved moderately successful, luring defectors from the three main ruling coalition parties. It is also actively courting disillusioned voters from the Five Star Movement, a key ally in a broad but perennially fractious leftwing coalition led by the Democratic party.

For the government, he represents a dilemma. Meloni, whose Brothers of Italy has neofascist roots, has governed more moderately than many had expected, cultivating a pragmatic and, crucially, pro-Ukraine image abroad while still deploying hardline rhetoric on choice occasions for domestic audiences.

That positioning, however, has left a vacuum on the far-right that Vannacci has exploited. The question now is: how will Meloni respond? Until now her ruling coalition had mostly coasted along, propped up by a strong parliamentary majority. Her government is largely regarded to have been fiscally prudent, but has steered clear of major structural reforms. Instead, it has heavily focused on security and continues to vigorously expand legislation on law and order.

“This government has wasted the huge occasion that stability gave them,” said Lia Quartapelle, an MP with the Democratic party. “None of the core issues have been addressed – we have stagnant productivity and growth, salaries that have lagged behind for many years and an education system that is not up to the pace.”

Pastorella said a focus on foreign policy had also contributed to Vannacci’s success. “Meloni hasn’t really done much at home but has been very present abroad,” she added. “The Italian electorate is tired of talking about foreign policy and would rather discuss national politics – this is precisely what Vannacci has understood.”

Picaro, the Brothers of Italy MEP, batted away questions about recent polls. “This is a government that is more used to working than looking at percentages,” he said, citing lower unemployment, reduced irregular immigration, cutting taxes for the self-employed and an initiative in the south to boost entrepreneurial investment.

Pastorella said that, far from being strong and stable, Meloni had struggled to keep her coalition united while dealing with various scandals, including ones that led to both a tourism and a culture minister being forced to resign.

With the possibility of an election as early as April, time is now of the essence for the prime minister. In recent weeks she has pivoted back to hardline rhetoric, most notably in her reaction to the influx of migrants from Morocco into the Spanish north African enclave of Ceuta.

She is also trying to push through a highly contentious electoral law that would give a majority bonus to any alliance winning more than 42% of the vote, which critics say is aimed at increasing her group’s chance of victory.

If Vannacci continues to strengthen, Meloni might be tempted to accommodate him before the vote, a move that would risk repelling moderate supporters. Or she could clinch a post-election pact to maintain power, resulting in what many both inside and outside Italy would see as a frightening shift to the extreme right.

As government supporters head to Bari, Alessandro Cattaneo, an MP with Forza Italia, thinks it won’t come to that. “We in Forza Italia believe that Vannacci is too far removed from our political culture,” he said. “It would not be possible to govern with him … the coalition needs to continue to work seriously for the remainder of this administration and explain better to people what we have done. The best antidote to the extreme right is to show our seriousness.”

articles.title: Iran targets US bases as Israel warns sanctions could drive Tehran to ‘desperate steps’
articles.summary:
Air bases used by US in the UAE and Kuwait hit as the Israeli defence chief says Iran’s regime fears collapse due to economic pressures

Iran has continued to demonstrate an ability to target…

blocks.text: Iran has continued to demonstrate an ability to target bases in the Gulf used by the US despite six months of war and a new sanctions regime described by the Trump administration as an “economic D-day”.

As Iran’s military targeted US bases in the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait, despite threats of further strikes by the US president, Israel’s defence chief warned that economic pressures from the sanctions could lead Tehran to escalate to more “extreme measures”.

“This morning, the army hit the satellite communication systems, equipment depots and fighter aircraft hangars of the terrorist US army at the Ahmad al-Jaber air base in Kuwait with missiles and drones,” the Iranian military said on Thursday in a statement carried by state television.
The “location of forces and radar systems of the child-killing US army at the Al Minhad air base in the UAE were also attacked by missiles and drones of the army”, it added.
In a post on X, Kuwait’s ministry of defence said its air defences had intercepted missile and drone attacks during a “blatant Iranian aggression”.
The Kuwaiti statement came after the US allies Bahrain and Jordan said their air defence systems intercepted several Iranian air attacks on Wednesday.

Fighting between the US and Iran has increased this week after the US hit Iranian rocket launchers on an island in the strait of Hormuz on Sunday, claiming that Iran was planning to use them to shoot mines into the waterway.

The latest flare-up in the conflict comes amid little evidence that the Trump administration is succeeding in advancing its nebulous war aims either on the battlefield or via mediation, despite the US president’s repeated claims to have opened the strait of Hormuz to oil traffic.

Instead, traffic through the key maritime passageway remains far below prewar levels, with oil prices remaining stubbornly elevated ahead of US midterm elections. Oil prices jumped again on Thursday after the Iranian strikes.

Among the weapons Iran has used this week is its Kheibar Shekan medium-range ballistic missile system. The cheap and accurate missile can be launched within minutes and has become a staple of Iranian strikes.

The rocket’s solid fuel motor means it does not require lengthy fuelling. It can be deployed very quickly to avoid detection and can be armed with a powered and steerable final stage to help beat anti-missile systems.

Despite claims by the Trump administration that Tehran is running out of rockets, Iran continues to fire missiles that are considerably cheaper to produce than the US interceptors used to shoot them down.
Iran has claimed as recently as the end of August that it maintained both missiles stockpiles and the ability to manufacture them.

“Initially, some believed that Iran had only a limited number of missiles and that its stockpiles would eventually be depleted as the war continued,” the IRGC spokesperson Brig Gen Hossein Mohebbi said.

“However, that assumption proved incorrect, as Iran’s missile capability has remained sustained and its missile production has continued.” Mohebbi’s characterisation of Iranian missile stockpiles could not be verified.

The continued strikes came as Israel’s defence minister, Israel Katz, said that while the new US economic sanctions appeared to be effective, the increased pressure might lead Tehran into extreme measures.

“We see signs indicating that the heavy economic pressure they are under, and the fear of an uprising and the collapse of the regime, may push them to desperate steps,” Katz said at a ceremony for defence ministry employees.
The hawkish minister reiterated the threats against the Islamic Republic that he has made in recent months.

“An Iranian attack on Israel will free Israel from any existing constraint,” he said. “We will strike all of Iran’s national military and civilian infrastructure – including energy infrastructure – and push Iran deep back into the stone age.”

articles.title: Putin denies fresh mobilization campaign in Ukraine war
articles.summary: The Russian president said there was no present need to mobilize more men, describing the reports as Ukrainian "disinformation." Putin was speaking during an economic forum in Russia's east.

image.caption: Putin said he was grateful to countries which were making an effort to mediate a resolution to the conflictImage: Vyacheslav Prokofyev/Sputnik/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Russia is not preparing to mobilize more men to fight, President Vladimir Putin on Thursday, describing such speculation as Ukrainian "disinformation."
In 2022 and a few months after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Putin ordered the unpopular "partial mobilization" of reservists amid a string of military set backs.
The decision prompted an exodus of draft-age men from Russia and the Kremlin has since repeatedly denied plans for another mobilization.
"There is no scenario today that would require mobilization," Putin told a plenary session of the Eastern Economic Forum in Vladivostok.

"This is a disinformation campaign by the enemy in the run-up to the State Duma elections, aimed at influencing the outcome," he added, referring to Russian parliamentary elections later this month. "As is well known, our people enlist voluntarily and sign a contract."
Putin had already dismissed mobilization speculations earlier this week, calling such reports "utter nonsense" and an "information attack" against Russia.
What did Putin say about peace in Ukraine?
Putin once again claimed there was a chance for peace with Ukraine, but stressed the conflict must be resolved by Moscow and Kyiv.
His statements come amid intensified Russian attacks on the Ukrainian capital. Meanwhile, Kyiv has intensified its attacks deeper within Russia, striking online retailers and other civilian targets.
Russia launches missile and drone barrage on Kyiv
Putin thanked countries which were making an effort to mediate a resolution to the conflict. He said the US and China, among others, were ready to support a peace settlement.

"Ultimately, however, the problem must be resolved ​by the countries involved in the conflict — Russia and Ukraine. ⁠This ​is the correct ​approach. Yet, we are grateful ​to everyone attempting to ‌ contribute to a settlement. Is there ​a ⁠chance? In my view, yes, there is," Putin said.

Still, he went on to condemn Ukraine, saying warnings about risks to planes in Russian airspace amount to "state terrorism." On Tuesday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that his country's drones have made Russian airspace unsafe for planes.

blocks.caption: Putin was speaking during the Eastern Economic Forum in VladivostokImage: Vyacheslav Prokofyev/AFP

blocks.text: How has Moscow responded to Zelenskyy's airspace warning?
On Thursday, Russia's Transport Ministry said it has provided clarifications to foreign airlines about Russian airports' and airspace safety measures.
"They work very closely with us and ​understand all our rules, standards and how we ​ensure flight safety," Russian news agency Interfax ​quoted ‌Transport Minister Andrei Nikitin as saying.
He added that the clarifications were given in response to requests from foreign carriers.

On Wednesday, Russian aviation watchdog Rosaviatsiya stressed in a statement that the country's "air transport, its ground infrastructure, continue to operate ​normally, receiving and dispatching flights, including those of foreign airlines."
European and US carriers have avoided Russian airspace since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. However, other airlines from China, Turkey and the Gulf states still use it.

articles.title: PNP: Bonoan may not be released Thursday night pending records check
articles.summary: Despite the Sandiganbayan ordering the release of former Public Works chief Manuel Bonoan, the Philippine National Police (PNP) may still hold him temporarily on Thursday night.

blocks.text: Published September 3, 2026 10:10pm
Despite the Sandiganbayan ordering the release of former Public Works chief Manuel Bonoan, the Philippine National Police (PNP) may still hold him temporarily on Thursday night.
PNP spokesperson Col. Allen Rae Co said that they have already received a copy of the order from the Sandiganbayan and it is being processed by the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG).

“Makikita naman po natin sa order ang last sentence doon ‘unless he's being detained for any other lawful reason’, so ang ating CIDG will be doing their due diligence na titingnan po natin kung mayroon pang ibang outstanding warrant against him or if he's facing any other cases sa ibang division,” Co told reporters.

(You can see it in the order that the last sentence there is 'unless he's being detained for any other lawful reason', so the CIDG will be doing their due dilligence that; we will check if there is any other outstanding warrant against him or if he's facing any other cases in other divisions.)
Asked if it is possible that Bonoan will not be released tonight, Co answered in the affirmative.
Co said that after checking Bonoan's records, they will follow the court's orders and release him. The process should be done by Friday morning.

Bonoan has been detained at the PNP General Hospital due to his old age and medical conditions. Co said that they will do final medical checks on him but he would also be free to seek treatment wherever he wants.
“Based on the reports, nasa stable condition naman ang kanyang health,” Co said. (Based on reports, his health is in stable condition.)
Co said that since Bonoan is a free man, there would be no reason for the police to escort him anywhere.

The anti-graft court dropped Bonoan after he was removed from the plunder case against Sen. Jinggoy Estrada, in relation to the flood control scam. Bonoan, in turn, will serve as a government witness. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Impeachment prosecutors evaluating not just bribery article but witnesses list --Luistro
articles.summary: The House prosecution team is discussing ways to expedite proceedings at the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, including possibly dropping the Article on bribery.

blocks.text: Published September 3, 2026 10:09pm

The House prosecution team is discussing ways to expedite proceedings at the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, including possibly dropping the Article on alleged bribery in the Department of Education, and evaluating the list of succeeding witnesses.

“The many discussions that the impeachment team is holding, as a matter of fact, hindi lang yung [is not just the] concern about whether to present or not the article on bribery. Even the list of witnesses in the remaining articles are being re-evaluated,” lead prosecutor Representative Gerville Luistro of Batangas told reporters in an ambush interview on Thursday.
She added that they have not reached a final decision.
“So, concerning that article on bribery, I can only confirm that's part of our discussions. But no official stand yet kung ida-drop ba o hindi [whether to drop it or not],” she said.

Asked what factors the prosecution team will consider in arriving at a decision, Luistro replied, “Well, tinitingnan din natin yung nauna nating nai-present, kung satisfied ba tayo, na-establish ba yung mga facts which we want to be established. Ganundin yung importance noong articles.”
(We will look at what we have already presented, if we are satisfied, if we have established the facts which we want to be established. And the importance of the articles.)
Luistro emphasized that all four Articles of Impeachment are “equally strong.”

“So lahat sila ay malakas, lahat sila ay strong, but we have this confidential fund already na pertaining to both the OVP [Office of the Vice President] and the DepEd. Siguro we focus on something else,” she stated.
Luistro also said they are considering the timeline.

“We do not want to drag this impeachment trial too much because we understand that somehow, naapektuhan yung buhay ng mga Pilipino [it is affecting Filipinos' lives] and even the focus of the parties concerned. As for one, the prosecutors, the senator-judges, and even the defense,” she said.

“Narinig natin yung manifestation ni presiding officer na talagang medyo challenge na sila [We heard the presiding officer when he waid they are challenged] considering that three important functions are being addressed by the Senate at the same time: yung kanilang regular legislation, yung budget hearing for next year of course, and itong impeachment trial. So, kino-consider din natin yun [we are considering that] as part of the government. We do not want to spend too much time on this impeachment trial,” she added.
One way to expedite the proceedings, Luistro said, was for the defense to accept the prosecution’s stipulations.

“Pinipilit natin mag-offer lagi ng stipulation to shorten the presentation of witnesses for the prosecution. Yun nga lang, minsan ay they refuse to agree even to common exhibits. Kaya natatagalan,” she explained.

(We are always offering stipulations to shorten the presentation of witnesses for the prosecution. Only they sometimes refuse to agree even to common exhibits. That's why it's taking longer.) — BM, GMA News

articles.title: DFA reports fewer incidents in Ayungin Shoal due to provisional PH-China arrangement
articles.summary: A provisional agreement between the Philippines and China on resupply missions to Ayungin Shoal has led to fewer confrontations between the two sides in the area, the Department of Foreign Affairs…

blocks.text: Published September 3, 2026 10:03pm

A provisional agreement between the Philippines and China on resupply missions to Ayungin Shoal has led to fewer confrontations between the two sides in the area, the Department of Foreign Affairs said on Thursday.

According to Tina Panganiban-Perez's report on "24 Oras," House members asked DFA officials about its response to confrontations between Chinese and Filipino vessels in the West Philippine Sea during the Committee on Appropriations hearing on its proposed P35.17-billion budget for 2027.

“One of the important provisions is not to prejudice the positions that we have had. That means UNCLOS (United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea) and the 2016 Arbitral Award," Foreign Affairs Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro said.
"This is a provisional arrangement only in this particular shoal, the Ayungin Shoal, because this is with particular reference only to the Sierra Madre ship,” she added.
The BRP Sierra Madre has been run aground at the Ayungin Shoal and serves as a Philippine outpost in the area.
Philippine authorities conduct rotation and resupply missions to the shoal to relieve personnel of duty and bring fresh supplies.
The DFA said there were 16 rotation and resupply missions that were implemented without incident in the past two years.
The DFA also said that it was correcting the false information that China was spreading.

“Meron din po kaming pagkakataon para mag-issue ng formal protests when it comes to very specific statements of the foreign ministry and the Chinese government,” DFA Assistant Secretary Robespierre Bolivar said.
(We have moments to issue formal protests when it comes to very specific statements of the Foreign Ministry and the Chinese government.) —Jean Mangaluz/NB, GMA News

articles.title: Estrella: DAR moving ‘full speed’ to split collective land titles
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – Agrarian Reform Secretary Conrado Estrella III said on Thursday his agency is “moving full speed ahead” in breaking up collective land titles as the World Bank-financed project…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Agrarian Reform Secretary Conrado Estrella III said on Thursday his agency is “moving full speed ahead” in breaking up collective land titles as the World Bank-financed project nears expiry.

The Support to Parcelization of Lands for Individual Titling (SPLIT) project is an initiative by the Department of Agrarian Reform (DAR) partly funded by the World Bank – that aims to break up collective land titles covering 1.38 million hectares issued to over a million agrarian reform beneficiaries.
At a congressional budget hearing, Estrella said there are about 750,000 Collective Certificate of Land Ownership Awards (CCLOA) pending before DAR as the loan is set to expire in Dec. 2027.
“We might make it at 500 [thousand], or a little less, for this year, and then finish the entire thing by next year,” he told lawmakers.
Estrella said the project “is still a priority” of DAR, as he touted that his agency is “one of the best, if not the best, agencies implementing World Bank-funded projects.”
Speaking to the Inquirer after the hearing, the agrarian reform secretary said breaking up CCLOAs “is easy.”
“If it were only up to us, we would finish this right now,” he said in Filipino. “It’s the World Bank slowing things down because they are strict in the use of funds.”
Land reform is a contentious issue in the Philippines, an agricultural country where vestiges of Spanish colonial land ownership have endured for decades, concentrating land possession among a few.
About 47 percent of the country’s total land area is agricultural land, according to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations. /mr

articles.title: NBI confirms Chuangxing rebars used in collapsed Pampanga building
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Steel bars recovered from the rubble of a collapsed building in Angeles City, Pampanga, were traced to a steel manufacturing plant under investigation, the National Bureau of…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Steel bars recovered from the rubble of a collapsed building in Angeles City, Pampanga, were traced to a steel manufacturing plant under investigation, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) said Thursday.

The disclosure was made during the Senate Committee on Economic Affairs’ second hearing on the domestic steel industry, where lawmakers continued to examine the possible use of substandard steel products in buildings and other structures.
Sen. Risa Hontiveros, who chairs the panel, asked whether the bureau could confirm that the steel bars recovered from the collapsed Pampanga building indeed came from Chuangxing Steel Inc.
NBI Senior Agent, lawyer Zulikha Marie Conales confirmed the finding.
“We confirm, we were able to recover rebars from the rubbles of the (collapsed) building in Pampanga, Madam Chair,” she said.

The confirmation came amid ongoing investigation into allegations that Chuangxing, a Chinese-owned steel plant in Magalang, Pampanga, may have produced and distributed alleged substandard steel bars to different parts of the country and were later used in construction.
Chuangxing was raided and shut down on July 18 after authorities discovered allegedly substandard steel products and radioactive materials inside the facility.
The raid came weeks after the May 24 collapse of a nine-story building under construction in Barangay Balibago, which left 27 dead.

Hontiveros also asked Conales about reports that 70 percent of the defective steel used in a damaged building in Mindanao came from Sanjia, another steel manufacturing plant under scrutiny by authorities.
“We confirm, madam chair,” Conales said, referring to the NBI’s investigation of the site.

The NBI had earlier raided Sanjia’s 22.6-hectare plant at the Phividec Industrial Estate in Tagoloan, Misamis Oriental, where radioactive materials were found, prompting the temporary shutdown of the facility.
Hontiveros said the NBI’s findings raised concerns about where else the alleged substandard steel may have been used.
“Grabe po yun because then we need to think about saan pa napunta yung ibang ganoong klaseng substandard na products, saan pang ibang mga gusali dito sa ating bansa,” she said.
(That is alarming because then we need to think about where else those kinds of substandard products went, and what other buildings here in our country they may have been used in.) /dp

articles.title: Anthony Joshua's driver attempted overtake before fatal crash, trial hears
articles.summary: Adeniyi Mobolaji Kayode, 46, is charged with offences including causing death by dangerous driving and reckless driving.

blocks.text: Image source, Getty Images
BySimi Jolaoso
Africa Correspondent
The driver of a car carrying Anthony Joshua was attempting to overtake another vehicle when it crashed, killing two of the boxer's friends, a court has heard.
Adeniyi Mobolaji Kayode, 46, faces charges including causing death by dangerous driving and driving without a valid national driver's licence. He denies the charges.

The court was told that the group - who had been travelling to visit Joshua's father in Ogun State, near Lagos in Nigeria, last December - were asleep when Kayode lost control of his Lexus SUV while he overtook a moving truck and collided with a parked lorry.
Joshua's personal trainer, Latif Ayodele, and strength coach, Sina Ghami, died in the crash.
A second defendant Abubakar Adamu, 35, the driver of the stationary lorry the car collided with, denies a charge against him of obstructing the free flow of traffic.
Inspector Christopher Ajayi Taiwo of the Ogun State Motor Traffic Division told the court that by the time he arrived at the scene, both the damaged Lexus and the stationary lorry had been removed.
But debris from the crash and soya beans scattered on the road from the lorry's load were found by officers, he added.
The only items recovered from the Lexus were a logbook, painkillers and an energy drink, which were found near the driver's side, Ajayi said.

blocks.caption: Image caption, The former heavyweight champion was a passenger in the crash, which killed his team members Latif Ayodele (left) and Sina Ghami (right)

blocks.text: Image source, Social Media
The former heavyweight champion was a passenger in the crash, which killed his team members Latif Ayodele (left) and Sina Ghami (right)
The court heard police had yet to take a statement from Joshua following the crash.

During cross-examination, Kayode's lawyer questioned Ajayi over the lack of statement, to which he replied that "efforts are ongoing" and that he had not contacted Joshua because he "didn't have his number".
The trial was adjourned until 10 September.
Joshua, who was born in Watford, has family roots in Sagamu - a town in Ogun state, near the crash site.
After the collision, the boxer posted a tribute to Ghami and Ayodele on social media.
"I didn't even realise how special they are," he wrote.
"I'll just be walking with them and cracking jokes with them, not even knowing God kept me in the presence of great men.
"100% it's tough for me, but I know it's even tougher for their parents."

articles.title: Senate may revisit impeachment voting threshold amid changes in composition --Zubiri
articles.summary: Senator Juan Miguel “Migz” Zubiri said some senators are seeking to revisit the voting threshold for the impeachment case, citing changes in the composition of the Senate since the required vote was…

blocks.text: Published September 3, 2026 9:51pm

Senator Juan Miguel “Migz” Zubiri said some senators are seeking to revisit the voting threshold for the impeachment case, citing changes in the composition of the Senate since the required vote was set.

“There were some colleagues who want to revisit because at that time wala pa yung mga nawawalang senador ngayon kasi may nasa kulungan, isa at large. I think that is the issue,” Zubiri told reporters in a press conference on Thursday.
(There were some colleagues who want to revisit it because at that time, the senators who are now absent were still there—one is detained and one is at large. I think that is the issue.)
Asked if there were proposals to lower the threshold, Zubiri answered:
“Yes,” he said, noting some senators have concerns about the threshold, but when asked when it would be debated, he deferred to the presiding officer.
“Best person to answer is PO (presiding officer)," he said.
He also said he expects the issue could eventually be brought before the Supreme Court
“I’m sure someone will take it to the Supreme Court,” he added.
He further stressed that the matter should be debated publicly.

Meanwhile, Zubiri also defended the Senate’s decision to allow budget hearings to run alongside plenary sessions, saying the chamber would not be able to complete its workload if the proceedings were kept to the usual schedule.
The Senate is currently juggling three major activities: the impeachment trial, the 2027 budget process and its legislative agenda.

He said the Senate amended its rules to allow senators attending budget hearings during plenary hours to be recognized as present. The arrangement is intended to maximize the chamber’s working time and prevent delays in the approval of the national budget.
He noted that the Senate is targeting completion of the budget deliberations by October so that plenary action can proceed in November and the country can avoid a reenacted budget.
Zubiri said that without the simultaneous budget hearings and plenary work, the Senate could still have 12 departments left to tackle by October 23, based on Senator Joel Villanueva's estimate.
“Pagod na pagod”
Zubiri also acknowledged the strain of the Senate’s unusually heavy workload.
“I’m very candid so I just tell them how I feel. I’m just being honest. It doesn’t matter kung pagod na pagod na ako. If we have to work 24/7, we will work.”
(It doesn’t matter if I’m extremely tired. If we have to work 24/7, we will work.)

He said the remark reflected his candid assessment of the workload, noting that it is the first time the Senate has had to handle the impeachment proceedings, budget deliberations and legislative agenda simultaneously. He added that senators may not get their usual October break as they work to meet the demands of the impeachment case and the budget. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: ‘Supersized’ El Niño may become strongest ever recorded, UN says
articles.summary: 'El Niño is being supersized before our eyes. The science leaves no room for doubt: The planet is in uncharted waters, and those waters are heating up,' says United Nations chief Antonio Guterres

blocks.text: EL NIÑO. A ship transits the Panama Canal near the Gamboa hydrometeorological monitoring station as a lack of rainfall linked to El Nino affects the water levels, in Gamboa, Panama, on August 27, 2026.
Enea Lebrun/Reuters
'El Niño is being supersized before our eyes. The science leaves no room for doubt: The planet is in uncharted waters, and those waters are heating up,' says United Nations chief Antonio Guterres

items: The El Niño phenomenon is expected to intensify through 2027, potentially becoming the strongest on record, according to the World Meteorological Organization.
There is a near 100% likelihood that El Niño will persist until February 2027, driven by exceptionally warm Pacific Ocean temperatures, which could lead to extreme weather events globally.
The WMO is enhancing preparedness and early warning systems to help countries manage the impacts of El Niño, including potential food crises and shifts in global temperature patterns.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

GENEVA, Switzerland – The El Niño weather phenomenon is set to intensify further into 2027 and could be the strongest ever, raising risks of extreme weather into next year, the World Meteorological Organization said on Thursday, September 3.

The UN weather agency said its forecasts showed a near 100% likelihood that El Niño would persist through February 2027, fueled by exceptionally warm Pacific Ocean temperatures. This is the first time it has expressed such a degree of certainty, the WMO said.
“If this trajectory continues, it may be stronger than anything since our monitoring began. So literally off the charts,” WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo told a Geneva press conference.

El Niño is a periodic warming of sea surface temperatures in the eastern Pacific caused by weakening trade winds. It occurs every two to seven years and tends to last up to 12 months, causing intense rains and droughts across Latin America.
A very strong El Niño can significantly shift rainfall and temperature patterns worldwide, and fuel extreme weather, such as droughts and typhoons.
While it is a naturally occurring phenomenon and not directly linked to fossil fuel-driven climate change, it can be intensified by warmer ocean temperatures, which are.
“El Niño is being supersized before our eyes. The science leaves no room for doubt: The planet is in uncharted waters, and those waters are heating up,” said UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres.

Sample Pacific Ocean temperatures in this year’s El Niño — one of just four categorized in the top “very strong” bracket in records dating back to 1950 — are already more than 2 degrees Celsius (3.6 degrees Fahrenheit) above normal, the WMO said.
The event has already had an impact on soft commodities in tropical areas, causing a severe food crisis across Central America’s Dry Corridor.

It is set to peak towards the end of this year, the WMO said in a statement. But its effects will continue into 2027 and are set to leave higher global temperatures next year in its wake, WMO officials said.

“Normally after an El Niño event we tend to see a pulse in the global temperatures — a temporary one,” Wilfran Moufouma Okia, the WMO’s chief of climate prediction services, told reporters, referring to 2024, which was the hottest year so far. “2027 has the potential to be the warmest on record.”
The WMO said it was stepping up preparedness and early warning efforts in preparation to allow states to take early action, such as switching to drought-resistant crops in some places.

“WMO is committed to working closely with partners across the United Nations and humanitarian system to provide the climate intelligence and insights needed to support disaster management and climate-sensitive sectors like agriculture, health, energy and water resources,” Saulo said. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Pampanga helps ease floods at NLEx, tallies monsoon damage at P1.339B
articles.summary: CITY OF SAN FERNANDO, Pampanga — The Pampanga provincial government and the provincial chapter of League of Municipalities of the Philippines on Thursday (Sept. 3) wrapped up their efforts in…

blocks.text: CITY OF SAN FERNANDO, Pampanga — The Pampanga provincial government and the provincial chapter of League of Municipalities of the Philippines on Thursday (Sept. 3) wrapped up their efforts in easing floods on the San Simon segments of the North Luzon Expressway, where motorists were caught in gridlocks for up to 8 hours over the weekend.
Three dump trucks of sand and 1,500 sand bags were provided by the province, and close to 50 people were mobilized to redirect or siphon out floodwaters until Wednesday midnight.
The costs of damages on crops, fisheries, machineries and farm structures reached P1.339 billion, the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office said.
Vice Governor Dennis Pineda lent two machineries to pump out floodwater.

“We did our bit to hasten the flow of traffic to be able to minimize the disruptions to motorists and passengers, and the economy,” the vice governor said as Pampanga continues to struggle with the impact of constant rains brought by the monsoon and a series of weather disturbances.

On Thursday morning, the San Fernando-Santo Tomas-Minalin Tail Dike took on another damage, with a 60-meter section collapsing in Barangay San Nicolas in Minalin town, Mayor Philip Naguit reported in a live broadcast on social media.

Naguit said the damaged segment was part of the 100-meter eroded shoulder discovered by Vice Gov. Pineda in July, adding that the Department of Public Works and Highways stopped repairs when heavy monsoon rains began lashing out by mid-August.

This was the ninth damage that the tail dike sustained, the most serious being a 30-meter breach on August 29 when the Gugu Creek overflowed and rerouted to the San Francisco River. Strong currents washed away the check gate there.

As of Thurday, 256 villages in 18 towns remained flooded but water levels on downstream Pampanga River rose to critical levels, according to the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office.

The floods have affected 374,292 families or 1.204 million individuals, with 8,964 families (32,461individuals) remaining in 456 evacuation centers. At least 3,538 families (14,843 individuals) are being served outside evacuation sites. So far, the costs of assistance from government and private groups reached P191.5 million. /mr

articles.title: Feminist activist Gloria Steinem dies at age 92
articles.summary: The co-founder and consulting editor of Ms. Magazine championed the feminist movement from the late 1960s onwards and inspired generations of women

blocks.text: WOMEN'S RIGHTS. Gloria Steinem protests against the opening of the first United States branch of De Beers jewelry store in New York, on June 22, 2005.
Keith Bedford/Reuters
The co-founder and consulting editor of Ms. Magazine championed the feminist movement from the late 1960s onwards and inspired generations of women

items: Gloria Steinem, a prominent American feminist writer and activist, passed away at the age of 92, leaving behind a legacy of fighting for gender equality and women's rights for over five decades.

She co-founded Ms. Magazine and was instrumental in the feminist movement, advocating for issues such as abortion rights, equal pay, and domestic violence, while also emphasizing the importance of listening to women's stories.

Steinem received numerous accolades, including the Presidential Medal of Freedom, and continued her activism and writing well into her 80s, influencing generations of women and shaping the discourse on feminism.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

Gloria Steinem, the American writer, lecturer, activist, and organizer who fought for gender equality and women’s civil and reproductive rights for more than five decades, has died, her foundation said. She was 92 years old.
The co-founder and consulting editor of Ms. Magazine championed the feminist movement from the late 1960s onwards and inspired generations of women.
She died on Wednesday, September 2, her foundation said in an Instagram post on Thursday, September 3.

“From reluctant spokesperson to a beacon of positive change, hers is a singular journey — an American leader who can speak to us all,” film and theater director Julie Taymor said of Steinem in a 2017 New York Times interview.

Taymor directed the 2020 film “The Glorias,” depicting Steinem’s life across the years and based on her 2015 best-selling autobiography “My Life on the Road.” She was also the subject of a 2018 play, “Gloria: A Life,” and a 2011 HBO documentary, “Gloria: In Her Own Words.”
Steinem said she considered herself “an entrepreneur of social change.”

“I want to do justice to the women I meet, to tell their stories,” she told the New Yorker magazine in 2015. “It’s making connections, and using myself to listen, because we can’t empower women without listening to their stories.”

Steinem founded the National Women’s Political Caucus in 1971 with former US Representatives Bella Abzug and Shirley Chisholm and writer Betty Friedan, whose 1963 book “The Feminine Mystique” ushered in the second wave of feminism.
Among other groups, she also created the Coalition of Labor Union Women, the Women’s Media Center, Voters for Choice, and the Ms. Foundation for Women.
In 2013, then-president Barack Obama awarded her the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the highest US civilian honor.

With her signature long, blonde-streaked, center-parted hair and aviator glasses, Steinem was the glamorous, hip symbol of the feminist movement, which she emphasized should embrace women of every race.
“If you’ve suffered discrimination, you’re sensitive to it on every level. I learned feminism largely from Black women. Women of color basically invented feminism,” she told the New Yorker.

Steinem was born on March 25, 1934, in Toledo, Ohio, the younger of two daughters. Her father was a traveling antique dealer. Because the family moved frequently she did not attend school regularly until about seventh grade.
Her parents separated when she was 11, following which Steinem lived with and took care of her mother, who had a mental breakdown and suffered from depression.
The experience impacted Steinem’s views on social injustice and marriage, which she believed robbed women of choices and many of their civil rights.
“I’d already been the very small parent of a very big child, my mother. I didn’t want to end up taking care of someone else,” she was quoted as saying.
After graduating from Smith College, Steinem began freelancing as a journalist.

In 1963, she worked as a Playboy bunny for 11 days for a story for Show magazine. Her two-part groundbreaking expose, “A Bunny’s Tale,” detailed the poor pay and sexist treatment Playboy bunnies — originally waitstaff — endured. The story was made into a 1985 TV movie starring Kirstie Alley.
In 1968, Steinem helped found New York magazine, where her essay titled “After Black Power, Women’s Liberation” established her as a feminist leader at a time of roiling social change.

But it wasn’t until she attended an abortion speak-out in a New York church the following year that Steinem — who had had a then-illegal abortion in London when she was 22 — said her life as a feminist activist really began.

Ms. Magazine, which she co-founded in 1971, tackled abortion and other issues such as sexism, equal pay, and domestic violence — a far cry from the diet of beauty, cookery and supporting-your-husband topics that were the staple of magazines aimed at women.

An early issue included the names of 52 women, including Steinem, who had had abortions, and called for the procedure to be legalized ahead of the landmark 1973 Roe v. Wade ruling that recognized women’s constitutional right to abortion in the US for nearly half a century.
Steinem was often critical of the limitations of marriage. “Women are not going to be equal outside the home until men are equal in it,” she said.
She had no children of her own, and it was not until she turned 66 that she decided to wed — to South African businessman and environmentalist David Bale, the father of actor Christian Bale.

“I hope this proves what feminists have always said — that feminism is about the ability to choose what’s right at each time of our lives,” she said in a statement about the marriage. David Bale died of brain cancer in 2003.

Steinem continued working into her 80s. She wrote numerous books, including 1986’s “Marilyn: Norma Jean” about Marilyn Monroe, “Revolution from Within: A Book of Self-Esteem” about personal development, and books of essays.

She narrated and conceived the idea for an Emmy Award-winning documentary about child abuse, “Multiple Personalities: The Search for Deadly Memories,” for HBO in 1993 and produced the Lifetime film “Better Off Dead.” She also hosted “Woman,” a documentary series about violence against women, for the Viceland TV channel.

Author Carolyn Heilbrun — who penned 1995 biography “Education of a Woman: The Life of Gloria Steinem” — described her as “the epitome of female beauty and the quintessence of female revolution.” – Rappler.com

articles.title: Vance's Antichrist comments are a 'common belief', his friend tells BBC
articles.summary: The US vice-president recently mused with a Christian podcast host on whether the end of the world was nigh.

blocks.text: Recent remarks by US Vice-President JD Vance about the Antichrist and "the end times" are a "very, very common belief", one of his friends says.

Vance recently mused on his religious views while responding to a question on a Christian podcast. He said he would "not [be] shocked if the Antichrist was walking among us" and speculated on whether the end of the world was nigh.

His friend Rod Dreher, a conservative writer, rejected any suggestion that the comments would harm the vice-president. He told the BBC's Today programme: "Most Americans who are inclined to vote Republican already believe this stuff."
In his podcast comments, Vance also clarified that such thoughts did not preoccupy him.
In Christianity, the "end times" phrase refers to theories about what will happen at the end of the world. Many churches believe God has a divine plan for the end of everything.
Meanwhile, the Antichrist is seen as the enemy of God who appears during the final phase of the world's existence and takes it over.
Vance, who became a Catholic as an adult, reflected on these topics during a recent podcast discussion with Bryce Crawford, a US Christian podcaster.

"Do I think that we're in the end times? I don't know," he said in response to a Crawford question on the subject. "And I think that it's probably bad for me spiritually to focus too much on it, because there are, like, things you gotta do.
"I gotta be good to my wife. I gotta be good to my kids. I have to be as good of a leader as I can for the United States of America."
The vice-president continued by saying: "I think that there are, like, things about the world that make me feel, like, not shocked if the Antichrist was walking among us."
But Vance reiterated that he was preoccupied with being vice-president, explaining: "What I'm trying to focus on is doing as much of God's work as possible right now."
Reacting to Vance's comments about the Antichrist, Dreher said: "This might sound bonkers to someone who is outside the Christian religion, but it is a very, very common belief within Christianity."
He said his friend was simply reflecting that the world appeared to be going "crazy" through the rapid development of AI and ongoing conflicts.

Dreher, who was present when Vance was received into the Catholic Church, said Ronald Reagan had made similar comments when he was the US president, and that this was seen as "perfectly normal" by his voters.
Vance converted to Catholicism in 2019, then in his mid-30s, and has described how the Church resonated with his family and social values and his conservative politics.
Since becoming vice-president, he has occasionally tangled with Pope Leo and his papal predecessor Francis, on issues including the Trump administration's immigration policy.
Vance is due to appear behind the lectern on Thursday afternoon to deliver the first White House press briefing since the departure of Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt.

Pagasa warned of floods and landslides that may occur during severe weather conditions.
It also forecast 50 to 100 mm of rainfall over the following areas:

Mindanao, may have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with localized thunderstorms.
